<note>The author is discussing the North as a direction of judgment.</note> ...let it be the North, for from there comes all evil or punishment resulting from sin. However, its property in creation is to illuminate and give form to matter, an action in which it is necessary for a privation of the preceding form (if there were any) to intervene.

You see that the effects of these three Names of God, taken from His properties toward His creatures, are varied: namely, the first inclines entirely toward clemency and mercy; the last toward severity; while the middle one participates in both natures, yet is most inclined toward clemency. And to this middle one is assigned the essential name **Jehovah**, because it is also exercised in this world, both in punishment and in beneficence, but it is much more prone to mercy than to punishment; hence it is written: *The LORD <note>original: "DEVS Iehoua"</note> is long-suffering, great in kindness, forgiving iniquity and transgression, who by no means clears the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, etc.* Numbers 14.

From this enumeration, therefore, grace and mercy flow into the lower realms through its channel or "bright gate."

But we think it should be noted in passing, as some might ask: what use is this Cabalistic science to us, or how is it to be proved that this or that name of the <term>Tetragrammaton; the four-letter name of God (YHWH)</term> has this or that property, or an inclination toward clemency or severity? To which we respond: it is proved by the effect in the Hebrew text. Hence the property of the name **El** is openly explained by Moses in that he records that he extracted the gift of health from God for his sister Mary <note>Miriam</note> when she was suffering from leprosy in this manner: *El na rapha na la.* **El** means GOD of grace, **rapha** means heal, **na** means I beseech, **la** means her.

Over the fifth enumeration (which is **Geburah**) presides the Name of God **Elohim Gibbor** <note>God the Mighty</note>, in which property God is said to have drawn the elements out of turbid Chaos; and this denotes power, violence, severity, judgment, and the punishment of sinners. This property of God flows into the lower realms—namely into the world—the effects of plague, famine, war, plunder, and desolation; whence it is clear that just as the nature of the Tetragrammaton **El** promised every good to the creatures of the world, so **Elohim Gibbor** seems to announce every evil and turbid outcome, such as occurred in the extraction of the elements from chaos.

The sixth enumeration is **Tiphereth**, which denotes grace and ornament, beauty and delights; the Name of GOD assisting this one is **Eloah**, whence it happens that all those influences poured out from this Channel, or this path, or divine property, give form to the sun, rendering to it clarity, life, and light, and they adorn the heavens according to that passage in Job: *By His spirit He has adorned the heavens,* Job 26:13. And also: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and all the host of them by the breath of His mouth,* Psalm 33. From these influences later proceed minerals, of which the prince is gold; vegetables, among which Bread and wine are the princes; and animals, whose head in dignity is man, following the position of the sun in heaven.

The seventh Sephirah is called **Netzach**, namely Triumph or victory. Furthermore, it indicates charity and the love of justice, and from here also follow the influences of multiplication and generation. The Name presiding over this is **Jehovah Sabaoth**, the Lord of Hosts.

The eighth is called **Hod**, namely praise, honor, and beauty. The Name according to its property is **Elohim Sabaoth**, that is, GOD of hosts, yet not for rigor and war, but for piety, justice, and concord.

Over the ninth enumeration presides the Name of GOD **El Chai**, that is, the living GOD, or **Shaddai**, GOD almighty, or self-sufficient; and this enumeration is called **Yesod**, that is, Basis, foundation, redemption, and rest.

The tenth and final Sephirah is called **Malkuth**, that is, kingdom, church, empire, and the temple of GOD; hence the Psalmist says, *for the kingdom is the Lord's,* Psalm 22. The Name of GOD presiding over this is **Adonai**, the Lord, and this enumeration brings severity and servitude to those upon whom it flows.

From these things it can be seen that in all the properties or operations of the divine essence upon the world—whether for punishment and the scourge, or for beneficence—GOD is more prone to clemency and mercy than to severity; for in the property of His first Name, He extends His charity out of the darkness into the world, as a father to a son, whence also **Hermes Trismegistus** calls the world the son of GOD.

In the property of the second, through His wisdom, He is more inclined toward creating things than toward striking the created human race with a plague for their sins, as is explained by the words of GOD to the Israelites: *Behold, I send my angel before thee to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared; beware of him,* etc. Exodus 23. But I have shown elsewhere that this angel was Wisdom, which was sent to the Israelites for their preservation, yet with the precaution that they should not commit evil, because He says, *he will not bear your transgressions.* Whence it is clear that God is more inclined in this property toward doing good than toward the scourge. In the property of the third Name, severity and punishment are included, for the name **Elohim** is by its nature terrible; whence it happens that as the name of the first Sephirah, namely **Ehyeh**, related to the Father, is attributed to the Empyrean heaven, the place of the blessed and of rest; and...

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. 255

The influences of the first **Sephirah** <note>The Sephirot are the ten emanations or attributes in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note>, namely those which descend from the shining gate of **Keter** <note>original Latin: *Cheter*; Hebrew: "Crown"</note> or the Crown—over which presides the name **Ehieh** <note>Hebrew: "I Am," associated here with God the Father</note>—flow and glide downward into the first order of angels, the **Seraphim**. From there, they are further guided downward by that great angel **Metatron** into the **Primum Mobile** <term>Primum Mobile: The "First Mover," the outermost sphere of the universe in traditional astronomy which carries all other spheres</term>, granting it the power and vigor by which it turns the celestial orbs from east to west within the space of a single day. For this reason, Metatron is appointed as the overseer of the First Mover, from whom he liberally pours the essence and faculty of motion into the lower realms. According to the Kabbalists, *Ehieh* bestows the gift of being, and thus Metatron's office is to flow these virtues into all creatures. This is the reason why he is regarded as the "Soul of the World." In this action, the property of God signifies clemency and kindness toward the world.

The outflows of the second **Sephirah**, the shining gate called **Chokhmah** <note>original: *Hochma*; Hebrew: "Wisdom"</note>—over which the divine name **Yah** or **Jehovah** presides—fall into the order of the **Cherubim**. From that order, they are entrusted to the guardianship of the Archangel **Jophiel** (or **Raziel**, as others prefer), to be introduced through him into the **eighth sphere** <note>The sphere of the fixed stars, located just below the Primum Mobile</note>. From this sphere, they are poured forth into the lower regions, both celestial and elementary. By their power, the fixed stars—both within the Zodiac and outside its belt—are observed to act upon the lower world, producing various forms of life, especially of animals. This is why the Zodiac is named from the Greek word *Zoon*, which means "animal." Because of this, Cecco d'Ascoli <note>original: *Cichus Eſculus*, a 13th-century Italian encyclopedist and poet</note>, in his book on the spheres, asserted not ineptly that every animal on land and sea symbolizes and corresponds in nature with some sign of the Zodiac. Furthermore, Maimonides <note>original: *Moyſes Arabicus*, "Moses the Arab," referring to the Jewish philosopher Maimonides</note> says that every animate thing has a star in heaven flowing into it to protect and preserve its essence.

Indeed, since every heaven or sphere—and consequently all the stars within it—has its own great angel to move and govern it, and to guide the influences sent to it from God through the "intellectual heaven"; and since many principal leaders are subject to each of these royal Archangels, who have many legions of spirits of lower rank under their command, we therefore say that each of these spirits has its own peculiar office both in the heavens and in the elements. **Hermes Trismegistus** seems to confirm this in part in the third book of the *Pimander* <note>A foundational Hermetic text</note> with these words: *The gods were seen in the forms of the stars with their signs; the stars were numbered according to the gods who inhabited them,* where by "gods" he seems to mean spirits or daemons.

The influence of the third **Sephirah**, which is **Binah** <note>Hebrew: "Understanding" or "Prudence"</note>—over which the divine name **Elohim** presides—passes through the order of the **Thrones** and is received by the Archangel **Zaphkiel** (or **Jophiel**, as others have it), who guides it into the **sphere of Saturn**. There it possesses its own peculiar virtue and property, distinct from the other planets. From here, this planet pours Saturnine influences, or Saturnine spirits and species, onto the earth, especially at the time when it holds dominion in the sky; for then its effects in the elements appear more evidently. These effects are for the most part gloomy and hardly favorable to the world or the human spirit; hence, it is called the **Greater Misfortune** <term>Greater Misfortune: In astrology, Saturn is the "Greater Malefic," associated with hardship and restriction</term> by astrologers.

The influences of the fourth numbering or shining gate, called **Chesed** <note>original: *Cheſed*; Hebrew: "Mercy" or "Clemency"</note>—over which the name of God **El** presides—descend into the order of the **Dominions**. Through them, they are carried downward by the Archangel **Zadkiel** into the **sphere of Jupiter**, which mercifully tempers its nature. As a result, the flows sent down from it are benevolent and gracious to both the air and the human spirit, as they are said to nourish and cherish natural strengths. Hence, it is called the **Greater Fortune** by astrologers.

The influences of the fifth shining gate or numbering, called **Gevurah** <note>original: *Geburah*; Hebrew: "Severity" or "Strength"</note>—that is, "Punishment"—over which presides the name of God **Elohim Gibor**, penetrate through the order of the **Powers**. They are guided by the Archangel **Camael** (or **Samael**) into the **sphere of Mars**, where they animate the fiery spirits of Mars with a burning and inclement severity. For this reason, this planet is not without cause called the **Lesser Misfortune** <term>Lesser Misfortune: In astrology, Mars is the "Lesser Malefic," associated with conflict and heat</term> by astrologers. Just as Saturn's influences usually act harshly upon the world's elements and creatures by way of extreme cold and dryness, so do the Martial spirits, bearing arms under the leadership of Samael, afflict the fiery air of the world with conflagrations, lightning, comets, and many other troubles, and infest the human spirit with heat, fever, plague, and inflammations.

The sixth shining gate is called **Tiphereth** <note>Hebrew: "Beauty" or "Grace"</note>, over which the name of God **Eloah** superintends. It flows through the order of the **Virtues**, and the Archangel **Michael** is by office the receiver of its influences. He translates them into the **sphere of the Sun**, from whose golden world gracious, splendid, and life-giving virtues are poured into the lower realms. These are called Solar spirits, which never act maliciously unless they are corrupted by the spirits of wicked planets.

The seventh Sephirah, called **Netzach** <note>original: *Netzeth*; Hebrew: "Victory" or "Triumph"</note>—to which is assigned the name of God **Jehovah Sabaoth**—sends its benevolent breaths into the order of the **Principalities**. From there, they are guided downward by the Archangel **Haniel** into the **sphere of Venus**. Thus it happens that the spirits of Venus emit favorable breaths into these lower regions; for this reason, Venus is called the **Lesser Fortune** by astrologers, being second only to Jupiter...

The Kabbalists <note>original: "Cabaliſtæ"; practitioners of Jewish mysticism</note> also wisely signified this whole matter through the differences of the various titles attributed to GOD within the sacred context. Just as these are various terms, wise men have observed that they produced different effects in the passages cited in the Bible. Because of this, they assigned various luminous properties to these names, which they believed descended through as many "shining gates"—each differing in quality—as there are names.

And they called these gates the **Sephirot** <term>Sephirot: In Kabbalah, these are the ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite reveals itself and interacts with the universe</term>, or the "enumerations" of the Kabbalists. They describe some of these as leaning toward severity and others toward mercy <note>original: "clementiam"</note>, depending on the nature of the subject being discussed in the holy text where those divine names appear. 

From these properties of God, they therefore observed that He is either severe and inclined toward the cursing of the world and humanity, or toward the blessing of those creatures. For this reason, they attribute the name and assign the role of both **destroyer** and **preserver** to Him.

### CHAPTER VII.

#### Concerning the **Angels of the Sephirot**, and primarily concerning that great and imperial **Angel of light** called **Metatron**, and then afterwards concerning that great **Angel of darkness**, who is opposed to him in nature and disposition.

From the dual arrangement of divine properties poured out from the Sephirotic <term>Sephirot: the ten attributes or emanations in Jewish Kabbalah through which the Infinite expresses itself</term> parts, two orders of Angels arise, opposite in nature and condition. One of these is occupied with benevolence, while the other is occupied with malice toward the human race, which is the goal of creation. 

And upon this foundation those philosophers were established who placed two principal powers in the world—namely, **strife** and **friendship** <note>This refers to the Pre-Socratic philosopher Empedocles, who argued that Love (Philia) and Strife (Neikos) were the driving forces of the universe</note>—the latter of which reconciles things, while the former scatters them. Hence it came to pass that, just as it was the role of **Apollo** <note>original: "Apollinis"</note>—according to the intention of the Poets—to compose and unite with the bonds of harmony, so indeed it was the property of **Dionysus** <note>original: "Dionysii"</note> to destroy composed things through the antipathy of discord, and to dissipate those things that were united. 

And yet, both **Apollo** and **Dionysus** represented nothing other than a single divine essence, emitting the operation of its act in a twofold manner and according to its own will—namely, either in clemency and piety <note>The text ends mid-sentence, likely continuing to describe the "severe" or "dark" aspect of the divine will on the following page</note>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the metaphysical and efficient causes of natural phenomena, specifically linking the "Efficient Cause of Meteors" to the divine emanations and the angelic hierarchy described in both Kabbalistic and Neoplatonic traditions.</meta>

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. 261

The Crown <note>original: "corona"; referring to Kether, the first Sephirah in the Kabbalah</note>, that primary emanation by whose power all things were brought from nothingness into being and action in the blink of an eye—this very emanation is called **Wisdom** <note>original: "sapientia"; in Kabbalah, Chokhmah</note>. From this, a second outflowing later issued through the "shining gate," emerging directly from the secret bosom of the Almighty. The wise man <note>King Solomon, traditionally the author of the Wisdom of Solomon</note> seems to confirm this elsewhere, saying: **Wisdom is a pure emanation or certain flow of the brightness of the almighty God, or the splendor and purity of eternal light. Wisdom 7.** And from this, it follows that this God-like Angel—that emanation or flow of divine majesty—is understood as the spiritual Christ, as stated before. In him, the angels find their end, as if in their own king, who contains and embraces both the nature of angels and of God, and in whom all other things are bounded. 

It is for this reason that the Kabbalists <note>Practitioners of Jewish mystical tradition</note> say the angel **Metatron** is the **Prince of Faces** <note>original: "facierum Principem"; a high-ranking angel who stands in the immediate presence of God</note>, because he is the mediator who introduces souls before the face of God. This is the office of the spiritual Christ himself, who is the true Wisdom, having first proceeded from the mouth of the Father like a son. The Prophet seems to understand this Angel when he says: **And his name shall be called the Angel of Great Counsel, Isaiah 6.** <note>The author is citing a version of Isaiah 9:6 often found in the Septuagint and early Christian theology</note> In this respect, this angel is accepted in many places of Holy Scripture as representing Christ. 

The more esoteric theologians <note>original: "Theologi secretiores"; referring to occultists or mystical philosophers</note> maintain that this is the angel to whose guardianship God committed Moses and the Israelites, to lead them through the wilderness, and in whom the name of Jehovah dwelt. They say he holds dominion in the world in the same way that the Mind—which is the Intellect—is said to rule in the human spirit. Regarding this power, specifically his expanded and universal authority, a man profound in hidden Divine Wisdom <note>original: "Theosophia occulta"</note> broke out into these words: **First among all is that great spirit, who directs the immense and most widely extended water, which is called heaven, and preserves it in his essence, and wonderfully grants motion to all growing and living things.**

This is why the Platonists and other wise men consider him the **Soul of the World** <note>original: "mundi anima"</note>, which the Kabbalists understood as the **green line** <note>original: "lineam viridem"; a reference to the 'Kav ha-Yarok' which encompasses the universe</note> said to circle the entire spirit of the world. From this, some conclude that this Angel Metatron is the final **Middah** <note>original: "Midah"; a Hebrew term for a divine attribute or measure</note> or property of the Archetypal World, which others call **Kether Elyon**, that is, the **Supreme Crown**. Thus, the name Metatron carries the meaning of "Gift of God"; for the life and form of the world was the greatest of God's gifts, including all other gifts within it. Therefore, all those skilled in mystical philosophy seem to arrive at this opinion, agreeing with the saying of Ecclesiasticus: that just as Metatron (or this Soul of the World) is the first thing created among all creatures, so he is said to contain within himself the perfection of all creatures, since they receive their forms from him as if from a universal fountain.

For this reason, Rabbi Moses <note>likely Maimonides</note> says that this Angel Metatron is the "Prefect of the Universe," or the primary **Active Intellect**, from whom all forms flow, and consequently by whom all individual powers in the world—and human ones especially—are governed. Rabbi Bereshit <note>A reference to authors of the Midrash Bereshit, or "In the beginning"</note> called all these powers "angels," while others called them "forms." Those who wish to see the mystery of angels (created together with natural things) contained under the common name of **Michael** as a name for the angelic species, seem to imply the same thing: that all angels are of the same species. 

We say, therefore, that whether the angel is called Metatron or Michael, he is nothing other than the white and pure emanation or power of God, which we previously called Wisdom. This emanation is clothed in the worldly spirit, which is illuminated by its presence as if by a garment. The Kabbalists hold this to be the power of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> wrapped in the worldly spirit from the world's beginning, just as the Messiah himself was clothed in flesh in the middle age of the world. 

Hence, Metatron is called an "Angel" insofar as there is "otherness"—that is, he consists of the created worldly spirit as an external part, and the uncreated divine spirit (the pure brightness of God or the emanation of brightness) as his internal part. This internal spirit is present everywhere in the world, filling, permeating, and producing all things, as it is the Word of God creating all. For this reason, esoteric theologians consider him the spiritual Christ or Messiah, or the power of the Tetragrammaton, as said before. The wise man in Ecclesiasticus understood this when he said that Wisdom was created before all things—that is, mixed into the worldly spirit in the manner of a creature. In this state, expanded everywhere, he established the heavens with their regions and the earth, gave them life, and brought them into being during the first three days of creation, according to the opinion of Moses. This is why we have it written by the Royal Psalmist: **By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm (and elsewhere: by his wisdom) and all their power by the spirit from his mouth.**

When the third day was completed, Metatron (whom for the reasons mentioned the Platonists called the Soul of the World) gathered his rays, which had been dispersed everywhere, into one polished mass of the world—namely, into the **Sun**. This was done by the divine outflowing of the **Ein Sof** <note>The Infinite/God</note> or infinity itself, operating through the gate of **Tiferet** <note>the Sephirah of Beauty, associated with the Sun</note>. This matches the Royal Psalmist's words: **He placed his Tabernacle in the sun.** Therefore, as Metatron somewhat changed his quality, the name **Michael** was also given to him, as reported before, as if one were to say, "Who is like God?" This argues that he is God himself putting on a garment of light, who animates the sun, and who for this reason is called the father of life and multiplication. Hence, David also said that God is **clothed with light as if with a garment**. In this respect, he is sometimes called an "angel" and sometimes "Jehovah," the reason for which Jehovah himself gave, saying: **Behold, I send my angel before you... do not provoke him, for my name is in him.** For all Kabbalists agree that this angel was Metatron or Michael. By the same reasoning, *Metatron* is said to have been the leader of Moses, through whose mediation it is handed down that Moses attained the grace of speaking with God face to face, as mentioned above: *I speak to him mouth to mouth* <note>original: "Ore ad os loquor ei"</note>, (says Jehovah to Aaron and Mary). He always holds the dragon, or the prince of darkness, under his will and command. Therefore, we read in Daniel that Michael is always an aid to the people of God. And just as we observe the sun to be the lord and as it were the commander of the whole heaven, giving life and light not only to its spirit but also to all its stars—which are said by the more excellent Philosophers to have received their luminous power and act of existence and essence from it, not otherwise than an earthly Emperor is accustomed to grant dignity and power of action to the minor kings, princes, or magistrates subject to him—so indeed we see here that this imperial angel, bearing a solar figure in his countenance, holds seven stars in his right hand. Indeed, in this way, Satan—the dragon against whom we read that **Michael** acted so valiantly and with such triumph in war—is the devastator of lives, the exterminator, the open enemy of salvation, the foe of the generation of man, and the persistent accuser and slanderer of souls before God. Many names have been given to this head and leader of malignant spirits by the Sacred Scriptures, encompassing great hidden mysteries regarding his condition. In the first place, he was called **Lucifer**; for such was he made in his origin by the Creator—namely, brighter and more splendid than the other angels, as Gregory <note>Likely St. Gregory the Great, a foundational theologian on the nature of angels</note> seems to assert. But truly, the goodness of almighty GOD is clearly declared in this: that just as He saw best and foreknew that sin was to be introduced into the world before anything was introduced into the world, and for this reason ordained the Devil from the beginning to punish it, so indeed His mercy so far prevailed over severity that He created and established good angels of ineffable virtue, and especially a single most powerful Prince, <note>Likely a reference to the Archangel Michael.</note> who is able to so overcome the Devil—who destroys the creatures of GOD—with strength and power, that in battle he not only drove him from the kingdom of the heavens, but also rules over him in that sublunary world. He <note>the Devil</note> is subjected to the pleasure of that Prince, who would restrain and hinder the evil spirits of the winds in their malevolent duties, and also correct the malignancy of those blasts according to the divine will, and direct them to prosperous effects by his infinite virtue, whose role it is to give life to all things, to preserve all things, and to cherish them. And this we have gathered most clearly from the Apocalypse: *And I saw four angels (says the Revelator) standing on the four corners of the earth, that they should not blow upon the earth, nor upon the sea, nor on any tree, and I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the Sun, having the seal of the living GOD, and he cried with a loud voice to the four Angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, saying: do not hurt the earth and the sea, nor the trees, until we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads, Revelation 7 etc.* By which he seems to intimate that that great and good Angel ascending from the east, whose task it was to preserve those whom GOD had chosen from the injury of the said malignant spirits and their angels, had power and empire over those destroying spirits; for at his command they immediately offered obedience. Now, in what manner these spirits appointed over the evil winds hold the reins of the winds, and how they are subjected to the command of the four great Angels of God, we have delineated in a visual description of this kind.

In another way, the inner man is said to be made in the image of God, and holds a superintendence over all other things; and just as a primary place is given in the heavens to the Sun—the highest and first in dignity of all the planets—so the Eastern angel, being dedicated to the sun and for this reason preferred over the others in dignity and rank, is said to be led by **Michael**, who is of the side of clemency. However, the Archangel **Raphael** rules the region opposite to him and its spirit, namely the prefect of the West Wind <note>original: "Favonii," the Roman name for the gentle West wind</note>, just as **Gabriel** rules the Northern region and **Uriel** the Southern. We also have this same point confirmed among the Hebrew Teachers: For Rabbi Taedacus Levi, in his *Book of the 10 Numerations*, after explaining the four winds—Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western—finally continues thus: *From those four winds he created four Angels who are set over them by day and by night. Michael, who is of the side of clemency and mercies, is appointed as the governor <note>original: "mamona," here meaning a prefect or official</note> over the East wind; until mid-day and until night, Raphael rules the West wind, who is likewise of the side of clemency. Then Gabriel, by the power of judgment and severity, is prefect with the North wind over half the night and two measures of the world; Noriel presides over the South:* so he says. But each of these has beneath him an Angel of the nature of a Prince of the air, each of whom has several species under him, which the *Book of Secrets* contains. This also seems to be confirmed by what is read in the *Gate of Light* <note>original: "Porta lucis," likely referring to the *Sha'are Orah* by Joseph Gikatilla</note>: *From the earth,* it says, *all the way to the firmament there is no empty space, but all is full of forms; some of them pure, some capable of grace and mercies, and there are many false, harmful, and tempting images below, all dwelling and flying in the air; some for peace, some for war, some for good, some for evil, some for life, some for death, and consequently some for safety and health, and some for sickness and infirmity. And all this is in the lower habitation in which we exist,* as Joseph Castaliensis asserts. From this it is clear that good Angels are intermingled with the foul and evil, so that the actions of the wicked demons (who hold God and men in ineffable hatred) may be tempered, repelled, and mitigated. And Bartholomew seems to support this assertion of ours, speaking thus: *The entire effort of demons or wicked spirits is to do harm, and to disturb and infest men with malice; for this reason they very often disturb the elements, stir up storms in the air and water, and corrupt the fruits of the earth, as is explained in the Apocalypse; and they would bring far greater evils upon the inhabitants of the earth, unless the good Angels blunted the edge of their violence.* From this, therefore, it is clear that they can do nothing except by divine permission, seeing that the good Angels are as bridles to them; but once permission is given, the good Angels themselves not only cease from their protection, but are even accustomed to contribute to the punishment of creatures, as we read everywhere in sacred scripture. Regarding the protection of good Angels against the assaults of evil Angels, the royal Psalmist speaks thus: *Fear not the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day, nor the plague that invades in the darkness, nor the attack of the noon-day demon; no scourge shall come near your tent, for he has given his Angels charge over you in all your ways, Psalm 91.* By this speech he clearly seems to hint that God has ordained to defend good men from the assaults of wicked demons through angels contrary to their natures. But this is elegantly demonstrated through the protection of the Archangel Raphael in the story of Tobias, who, by repelling the assaults of the demon Asmodeus, preserved Tobias immune from his rage.

We conclude, therefore, that it is most certain that just as Lucifer, now called Satan, after his fall and exile from heaven was made the universal Prince of this air, according to the saying of St. Paul, his primary effect is from the South—which is the place from which rot is sent out, and where plagues, wasting diseases, and thunders are very often emitted. Hence he is called by the Hebrews (as was declared before) *Meririm*; that is, the demon burning and raging at noon: Or as Habakkuk and the royal Prophet say in the places cited before, the pestilence or the demon wasting at noon or in the South. So, just as this Prince of the air divides his aerial kingdom into four quarters—namely East, West, South, and North—and assigns a prefect to each part by divine command, whose duty is to make the winds blow perversely; so indeed was the mercy toward the things created in the sublunary heaven, and especially toward man, so great that in place of that Prince of great wrath and malice in the air or this world in which we live, He placed a Prince yet greater and full of graces and clemency. This Prince also has three other angels joined to him as companions, similar in property and goodness, who have force and power over those spirits acting as deputies of Satan who have power over the winds. Hence, just as Meririm with his spirit is accustomed to rage in the South, so Michael the great Prince, who has superintendence over the East <note>original: "Metirem," likely a typo or variant for "orientem"</note>, claims for himself the eastern corner of the world, in which he takes care of the actions of Samael or (as others say) of the East, as has been said more often. For these are the words of Cornelius Agrippa: *Book 3 of Occult Philosophy, chapter 24. Among the evil spirits, four most powerful kings preside over the others according to the 4 parts of the world, whose names are Uriens or Oriens, king of the East; Amaymon, king of the South; Paymon, king of the West; and Egyn, king of the North. The teachers of the Hebrews perhaps more rightly call them Samael, Azazel, Azael, and Mahazael, under whom many other princes and presidents rule, as well as innumerable demons of private offices.* So he says. And yet in his Scale of the number four <note>A reference to a table of correspondences in Agrippa's work</note> he says: *There are four Angels presiding over the corners of heaven: Michael over the Eastern, Raphael the Western, Gabriel the Northern, and Uriel the Southern. There are four Prince demons harmful in the elements: Samael, Azazel, Azael, Mahazael. There are four Princes of demons over the 4 corners of the earth: Oriens, Paymon, Egyn, Amaymon.* From which it is clear that this author is not consistent with himself, since he makes a difference here between the four princes harmful in the elements and those over the four corners of the globe, who have the care of the winds...

...are said to be: Furthermore, in that same scale <note>The author refers to the "Scale of the Quaternary," a Renaissance concept where things are grouped in fours to show the harmony of the universe.</note> he says there are four Prefects of the elements: namely, **Seraph** for fire, **Cherub** for air, **Tharsis** for water, and **Ariel** for earth. But to show our own opinion on this matter, we say that it is more probable to consider that, since the wheel of the sublunary <note>The region below the moon, consisting of the four changing elements: Earth, Water, Air, and Fire.</note> spirit is filled as much by the goodness of God as by the malice of the Devil, it seems likely that every element has its own **good** and likewise **evil** Prince. Both are ministers of the divine character; for God uses the good prince to do well through mercy, and the evil one to punish and do harm through severity. Therefore we say that just as there are four good princes—**Seraph, Cherub, Tharsis,** and **Ariel**—so there are evil and vengeful ones: **Samael, Azazel, Azael,** and **Mahazael** in those same elements. And since the Winds participate in the Elements—namely the East wind in fire, the North in earth, the West in water, and the South in air—therefore the elementary Spirits, both evil and good, receive their strengths from the Spirits of the winds, whether blowing for good or ill. From this, it is certain that the East Wind <note>original: "Ventum Eurum"</note> shares as much in the heat as in the violence of **Samael**, and so it is with the others. We also affirm that the royal spirits on the side of Satan who have power over the winds—namely **Oriens, Paymon, Egyn,** and **Amaymon** <note>These names frequently appear in medieval and Renaissance grimoires as the four kings of the cardinal directions.</note>—are subject to the commands of those good angels who preside over the quarters of the world, namely **Michael, Raphael, Gabriel,** and **Uriel**. Above all, they are subject to that imperial Angel of goodness and life, **Michael**, who has power and authority over the Prince of darkness or the "dark air" because of the victory he won over the Dragon. Therefore, under his supreme command are all demons, whether of the Winds or of the elements, be they good or evil.

Here it must also be considered in passing that, according to the position of the gates in the heavenly city (of which three were situated toward the east, three toward the west, and just as many toward the north and south), the same holds true for the winds. For in every region of the world there are three winds: namely the **Subsolanus** (East wind) with its two wings, and the **Auster** (South wind) toward the south, and **Caecias** (Northeast wind) toward the north, and so with the rest, as you have clearly depicted in the demonstration above. And since, following the likeness of the gates of the heavenly Jerusalem, you have the Zodiac of the starry sky divided into four <term>triplicities</term> <note>In astrology, a triplicity is a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element.</note>—namely the Fiery and eastern, the Airy and southern, the Watery and western, and the Earthy and northern—three signs are assigned to each of these triplicities: **Aries, Leo,** and **Sagittarius** to fire; **Gemini, Libra,** and **Aquarius** to air; **Cancer, Scorpio,** and **Pisces** to water; and finally **Taurus, Virgo,** and **Capricorn** to earth. Similarly, because a specific prince of the Angelic nature is assigned to each triplicity, and a particular angel is assigned to each sign under him, it seems likely to me that not only is a Prince Angel ascribed to a cardinal point, but also to every "windy gate" in that region, which must have a relationship to its sign and the power it falls under. We have made mention of the demons of the triplicities and the peculiar spirits of each sign before, where we spoke of the demons of the Zodiac. We could indeed put together great volumes on this subject, but since we shall discuss these things more openly elsewhere, we will not speak more of them in this place.

You have here, benevolent Readers, how clearly described and vividly depicted are the two great Princes of intelligences, fundamentally different in character and nature. The first, who is the most powerful of all, is the **Angel of light**: merciful, good, the author of health and life, the solace and rest of the world, the driver-away of death and disease, who holds evil in hatred and cherishes and nourishes good benevolently. We have declared him to be the dispenser of divine mercy, benevolence, and kindness; the guardian of souls and even of bodies. From his region come those good angels of men whom we call the **holy and good geniuses** <note>In the classical sense, a "genius" is a guardian spirit assigned to a person at birth.</note>. He is the author and actor of the world's salvation and human resurrection (as one who obtained victory over the Devil and Death). The other Prince, however, is completely opposite to him in condition and will; for as the **Angel of darkness**, he is accustomed to seethe with severity and impiety. He delights in evil actions, is the author of diseases, pains, and destruction, the scourge and restlessness of the world, the destroyer of life, and the bringer of death into the world. He holds good in hatred and strenuously cherishes and nourishes evil. We have declared him to be the dispenser of severity, malevolence, and indeed of universal impiety, the destroyer of souls and bodies. Under his rule are those evil and wicked demons called **evil geniuses**. He is the author of the world's ruin and man's damnation. And so you see these two Angels are entirely contrary to one another in quality. Concerning these, therefore, I have decided to treat particularly in the following volume—where we shall discourse copiously on health and disease—and that with a more polished and clearer thread of discourse (God Most High being favorable).

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. 271

Vainly, therefore, did the ancient Magi attribute the actions of the one true God to demons; these actions are the works of the Lord God alone, <note>original: "DEI Iehouæ"</note> and such beings are by no means to be regarded as gods. This is the very root of the nations' idolatry mentioned in the Fountain of Truth, where it is read: *They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods whom they did not know,* <margin>Deuteronomy 32:17</margin> And this is the reason why an express law was given against the worship of demons at the very beginning of the Mosaic Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments</note>: and elsewhere we are warned that sacrifices are not to be offered to demons, as in *Leviticus.* <margin>17:7</margin>

Vainly also have astrologers attributed the movements, virtues, and operations of "influences" <note>In this context, 'influences' refers to the invisible forces believed to flow from the heavens to the earth.</note> to the stars, and especially to the Sun and Moon. These are actually the works of the Wisdom or the Divine Word, <note>original: "verbi Diuini"</note> and they could not exist at all without His life-giving gift. For this same error was a notable occasion for idolatry among the heathens and Gentiles. For example, the Egyptians worshipped the Sun, whose houses and statues the King of Babylon is said to have shattered. <margin>Jeremiah 43</margin> Furthermore, the Jews also fell into this damnable error, wherefore it is said that *the chariot and horses of the Sun were removed from before the temple of the Lord.* <margin>2 Kings 23</margin> <note>original: "4. Reg. 23." In older Latin Bibles, 1 and 2 Kings are titled 3 and 4 Kings.</note> And in another place, the Bible testifies that God created the Sun, Moon, and other things to serve all the nations under heaven; therefore He forbade them to be adored or worshipped. He commands the Israelites not to look upon the Sun, Moon, or stars, or any part of the host of heaven, so as to bow down and worship them. <margin>Deuteronomy 4</margin>

By these things we are taught that just as God is the sole author and actor in this world, so praise, honor, adoration, and worship are to be offered to Him alone and not to any created thing. Whatever might happen to us or to the world should not be derived from the creature, but from the power of the Creator and the act of His emanation. We should believe it proceeds within the creature and is sent forth from it as if from a vehicle; for the creature itself, without His act, is plainly dead, possessing no value or standing in itself.

But because it is the custom of the world to affirm—according to the doctrine of the ancient astrologers—that celestial influences and their virtues are derived from the stars, and consequently to speak with the heathens of Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Orion, the Raven, Cassiopeia, and others among the fixed stars, and Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, the Sun, etc., among the planets, as being the causes of this or that alteration in the air, earth, and water; for the better understanding of our readers, we will follow in their footsteps. We will name and call the planets and fixed stars the causes of storms and <term>meteors</term> <note>In the 17th century, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and lightning, not just falling rocks from space.</note> in the air. We do this, however, on the condition that we always hold in our memories that it is not the star we have named, but the divine influx sent from the divine <term>Sephirotic gates</term> <note>The Sephirot are the ten attributes or emanations in Kabbalah through which the Infinite reveals itself.</note> into the sphere and body of the planets. This influx is poured down into the lower realms by its angelic minister according to the will of the <term>En Soph</term> <note>The Infinite or Boundless nature of God before self-manifestation.</note>—or the Fatherly Infinitude—whether for the punishment or the benefit of mortals. This is the fountain and origin of effects of every kind produced in the air, water, and earth.

These things having first been considered by the true Christian, we will hasten to the description and living explanation of the triangle in our <term>meteorographic Mirror</term>, <note>A 'Catoptron' or Mirror was a term often used for a scientific diagram or a systematic summary of a subject.</note> in which meteorological forecasting is clearly expressed through the "aspects" <note>The geometric angles between planets.</note> of the planets relative to one another—namely the **conjunction** (signified thus: $\sigma$), **opposition** (signified thus: $\rho$), or **square** (signified thus: $\square$)—as they relate to the moon. The image of the Triangle is depicted below.

### CHAPTER II.

*On the changes of the air; on the origin of a comet; and thereafter, on various changes of the air according to the aspects—$\sigma$ (conjunction), $\rho$ (opposition), and $\square$ (square)—of all the planets, both toward the moon and among themselves.*

Astrologers say that the "efficient cause" of all species of Comets are the stars, both fixed and wandering <note>Planets</note>; and they generally warn us that meteors of this kind imitate the natures of Mars and Mercury. Hence, they say it follows that they signify war, heat, and tumult. Similarly, Ptolemy in his *Second Quadripartite* <note>The Tetrabiblos, a foundational text of astrology.</note> wishes for us to consider the stars which are accustomed (as he says) to stir up the matter and draw it along by their motion; he also teaches us to observe the place or sign of the Zodiac under which it is ignited.

As for the various changes of the air—regarding winds, clouds, rains, snows, hail, thunder, lightning, and other things—and regarding the exposition of the meteorological triangle depicted in our meteorographic Mirror, take note of this:

### CHAPTER III.

#### ->An explicit exposition on the wheel depicted in the empty right-hand region of our Meteorographic Mirror, and at the same time on the openings of the gates, sluices, and great floodgates.<-

For your better understanding, we have depicted this wheel here in this place so that, by looking at it, you may more easily understand the things contained within it. In this wheel, then—which is taken from our Meteorological Mirror or Reflecting-Glass <note>original: *Catoptro*</note>—one may see a twofold description: namely, the openings of the **great floodgates** of heaven, which are described in the upper sphere, and then subsequently the openings of the **gates** of heaven, which are revealed in the parts rotating around the center of the sphere. 

Regarding the openings of the great floodgates of heaven, it should be known that the sluices and great floodgates of heaven are said to open when the Moon, moving away from a conjunction, a square aspect, or an opposition with the Sun, Jupiter, or Mars, is led and passes directly to Saturn, Mercury, and Venus, or vice versa. That is, if the Moon, moving away from a **conjunction** <note>symbol: ☌; when two planets appear in the same spot in the sky</note>, a **square** <note>symbol: □; an angle of 90 degrees between planets, usually considered tense</note>, or an **opposition** <note>symbol: ☍; an angle of 180 degrees</note> with Saturn, Mercury, or Venus, is carried toward the Sun, Jupiter, or Mars; for then, according to the opinions of all astrologers, rains in abundance and, consequently, great floods are to be expected.

Similarly, the openings of the gates are to be gathered from the observation of the lower sphere. For where you observe in the order of the sphere a square line marked with □ between the Sun and Saturn, or the Moon and Saturn, or Venus and Mars, or finally Mercury and Jupiter; or similarly a diametrical line of opposition marked with ☍ between the Moon and Saturn, or between the Sun and Saturn, or between Jupiter and Mercury, or finally between Mars and Venus; and finally, where you see the **Moon** <note>symbol: ☾</note> with **Saturn** <note>symbol: ♄</note>, or **Mercury** <note>symbol: ☿</note> with **Venus** <note>symbol: ♀</note>, or Venus with Mars with this sign ☌ (that is, in conjunction), they say the gates of heaven are open or about to be opened immediately, so that copious rains and showers are to be expected. 

For this is a secret observation among astrologers, and a science not much publicized by them. But indeed, Aomar <note>likely referring to the 9th-century Persian astrologer 'Umar al-Tabari</note> holds in his observations that if the Moon moves away from Venus and, after its departure, applies its rays to Mars, or if it moves away from Mars and applies itself to Venus, it then draws back the sluices of heaven; but if it moves away from Jupiter while applying to Mercury, or rather, having separated from Mercury it proceeds to Jupiter, it opens the gate here once more. So says he. 

But that which we previously condensed and organized into the aforementioned sphere (having been proven by long experience), we hold in the highest value; consequently, we believe it should be preferred by far over the precepts of others. Nevertheless, use your own judgment, and I advise you to follow what seems more probable to you in this matter. Regarding the remaining celestial signs of weather change, we have spoken more fully in our **Astrological treatise** described in our *Technical History* <note>likely referring to the author's own multi-volume work, such as Robert Fludd’s *Utriusque Cosmi Historia*</note>, so I think you should be referred to that place.

### CHAPTER IV.

->**Concerning the celestial efficient cause of the Winds, where our own opinion on the Winds is briefly introduced and supported by strong reasoning.**<-

After Fregius <note>Johann Thomas Freigius (1543–1583), a German philosopher and polymath.</note> made mention of the causes of the winds, he himself (led by better reason and departing from Aristotle’s opinion) spoke thus: "Although the entire dispute concerning the winds, as with other meteors <note>In this period, 'meteors' referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain and wind, not just falling stars.</note>, is full of the wonderful works of God—for which no firm and sufficient efficient causes can be produced in nature—nevertheless it is useful to see how far human reason can progress. Indeed, Holy Scripture says that God produces the winds from His treasures, from which we hear their blowing, but we do not know from where they come or where they go." This is what he says.

And indeed, both the Peripatetics <note>Followers of Aristotle’s school of philosophy.</note> themselves and Pliny—that diligent investigator of causes—are so wrapped in clouds of obscurity and ignorance that when they see themselves caught in the mire of ignorance, they attempt to excuse themselves in part with subtle and vain distinctions. They say some winds are miraculous—namely, those for which no cause in nature can be given. An example of this kind is the one described by Pliny, who says there is a certain cave on the coast of Dalmatia <note>Modern-day Croatia.</note> with a vast, steep opening. If a light object is thrown into it, even on a perfectly calm day, a stormy wind like a whirlwind is immediately observed to rise from it.

They also judge similarly those winds that burst forth from the rocks of the province of Cyrenaica <note>An ancient Greek and Roman region in modern-day Libya.</note>; for this reason, they hold those rocks as things so sacred that they believe they would be profaned by too much contact. For if they are touched by hands even once, the South Wind—<term>Auster</term> <note>The Latin name for the hot, dry south wind, often associated with the Sirocco.</note>—is immediately stirred up, swirling the sands; thus they have consecrated these rocks to the South Wind. 

But indeed, for those winds for which they could devise some cause within the possibilities of nature, they called these "natural," and judged their efficient cause in their own manner. From this, anyone can see how uncertain the opinion of men engaged in vain philosophy is regarding such deep matters, and how inconsistent the judgment of human wisdom can be.

Furthermore, even among the fathers of the Astrologers, there seems to be great hesitation and instability in their opinion regarding the efficient cause of the winds. For just as the Peripatetics divide their natural winds into "steady" and "sudden"—and divide the steady ones again (which they define as those that begin and end blowing at fixed times) into "general" or "principal" winds, namely those that usually blow from the four cardinal points <note>North, South, East, and West.</note>, and "particular" and "minor" winds, which are observed to blow in certain provinces—so indeed the Astrologers look deeper into...

<meta>This page continues the discussion on meteorology, specifically moving from the general definition of atmospheric phenomena to the specific "efficient causes" (the forces that create them) of winds, contrasting ancient philosophy with Christian and Hebrew mystical thought.</meta>

# On the Efficient Cause of Meteors. 277

Those ascending into the investigation of these causes have claimed that impetuous winds—whether sudden or general, and especially those that blow from the North <note>original: "ex parte Aquilonis"</note> toward the west—stem from the influence of Mars, and they say such winds are subject to him. Others, however, claim that winds are the "infant children" of the Sun, the Titan Astraeus <note>In Greek mythology, Astraeus was the father of the winds</note>, and Aurora <note>The Goddess of the Dawn</note>, insofar as they are generated by the sun's heat, which makes the air thin and rare, especially at dawn. Indeed, even Aristotle admits that winds are produced by the heat of the Sun. Yet all winds are said to receive the commands of Juno, because they do not blow except in the air, and "Juno" is another name for the air itself. Others say that among the fixed winds, those they call the *Prodromos* <term>Greek: "forerunners"</term> (as they precede the *Etesian* winds) blow during the most burning time of summer, around the time the Dog Star <note>The star Sirius, associated with the "dog days" of summer</note> rises, and they precede the Sun as it enters the first part of Leo by about eight days. Furthermore, the Etesians themselves, which are Northerly winds, are observed to blow constantly for forty days, and the "forerunners" precede them. Ptolemy is eager to attribute these winds to Jupiter, saying it is Jupiter who stirs them up, which is why he claims they are more fertile and healthful than the others. These begin to blow immediately after the solstice and the rising of the Dog Star, as Aristotle says; however, Pliny says the Etesians begin two days after the rising of the Dog Star while the sun is in Leo, and so on for the others.

From this, you can see that there is such great difficulty in finding the causes of the winds that even the Philosophers themselves have been unable to judge anything certain or firm about them. Instead, whatever they do, they gather from the results and from long experience and practice; they see everything "from the effect" <note>original: "a posteriori" — reasoning from known effects back to unknown causes</note> and not "from the first principle" <note>original: "a priori" — reasoning from causes to effects</note>.

But we, as is fitting for a Christian, do not cease to scrutinize the mystery of the winds and other meteors in a more profound way. We do so not from Aristotle, nor from the book of any other Pagan <note>original: "Ethnicorum"</note> author who was ignorant of the acts of the Divine Word (through whom, according to the Bible—the fountain of truth—all things were made). Most of them were ignorant, though the "Divine Plato" is always to be excepted. Instead, guided by the instruction of the Holy Scriptures, and at the same time by the infallible reason and demonstration of philosophical probability, we have immersed ourselves (not without great delight) into the most internal cause of these creatures. With every effort, we have sought out the opinion of the Hebrew Doctors on this matter, as it was their role to be more deeply engaged in the mysteries of the Jews, and especially in the exposition and interpretation of the Holy Bible. Indeed, Rabbi Tedaco Levi, who in his *Book of the Ten* <note>Likely a reference to a work on the ten Sephirot or divine emanations</note> numbers them, says: *Speaking of the four Cardinal Winds: From those four winds, God appointed four Angels over them by day and by night; Michael, who is from the side of Mercy, is appointed over the East wind; and Raphael rules the West wind. Then Gabriel, in the power of judgment and severity, is appointed over the Northern wind, and Noriel or Uriel presides over the South.* This is what he says. And in the *Book of Secrets* <note>original: "libro arcanorum"</note> we read that each of these has many legions under him, which they employ in their business to fulfill the will of the Creator.

However, considering the matter to its very core, we are forced to disagree with that Doctor on certain points. For it is certain and beyond all doubt, as proven by the experience of sailors, that the Frigid Zone of the Antarctic region of the world is no less stiff with cold and cold effects than the Boreal <note>Northern</note> region—namely with frost, snow, and constant ice. These effects are produced by the wind blowing from the Antarctic pole in no different a way than the cold effects from the North or Boreal winds. Therefore, it seems very unlikely that a "fiery spirit" such as Uriel—whose name means "Fire of God" <note>Hebrew: "Oriel" or "Uriel"</note>—or Meriris, which signifies a "burning demon of the noonday," would have dominion or power in that region where the pole star of the Antarctic hemisphere has its seat. For this is certain, and to be denied by no one: just as the Northern hemisphere is divided into its temperate and frigid land zones extending all the way to the pole star, so it is apparent that the opposite hemisphere is distinguished into just as many regions of similar condition. Specifically, the space of the Torrid Zone is that which is located between the Equinoctial line <note>The Equator</note> and the Tropic of Capricorn, and the temperate zone extends in latitude from the Tropic of Capricorn to the Antarctic Circle. Finally, they measure the Frigid Zone from the Antarctic Circle to its own pole star.

From these facts, it is clearly established that the wind blowing from the Antarctic pole is governed neither by Meriris nor by Uriel or Noriel, since it is contrary to fire by its nature and condition, being instead extremely cold. Therefore, we must consider, and quite seriously, that the more suitable seat for the aforementioned angels would be in the Torrid Zone...

## BOOK TWO.

### On the Elementary Efficient Cause.

### CHAPTER I.

#### How the regions of the world are compared to the visions of human sense, and that the more divinity immerses itself in the multitude, the more its rays are covered and hidden from human sense.

Just as three visions are observed to exist in man, of which one is corporeal and deals with bodily objects (in which the exterior sense is most often deceived by judging as true those things which are actually feigned and false images <note>original: "simulachra"</note>, such that this is the most uncertain of all human visions); the second is in the imagination or <term>phantasy</term>, which is the first degree of spiritual vision, in which the likenesses and, as it were, the shadows of bodies are perceived—for to the "phantastic spirit" <note>The "spiritus phantasticus" was believed to be a subtle substance in the brain that processed sensory images.</note> corporeal objects sometimes appear no differently than an image in a mirror. And this vision, inasmuch as it is a medium between the external sense and the intellect, sometimes sees false things and is deceived, but in looking toward the intellect it can hardly be deceived at all; therefore, this species of human vision is more certain than the corporeal one. Finally, the third species of vision is the intellectual one, which is accustomed to gaze upon things that are neither corporeal nor have the forms of bodies; the objects of this kind of human vision are the mind itself, **GOD**, justice, wisdom, and every good affection of the soul.

In a similar way, the matter holds true for men in the inspection of the efficient cause of meteors <note>In this period, "meteors" referred to all atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and lightning.</note>. For those to whom it is given by the vision of the intellect to look into and gaze upon the "marrow" or essence of meteors, they see indeed that God himself—the supreme mind, the word, or divine Wisdom—is the sole and infallible agent in their production; and that vision is truly intellectual. There is also another vision, which is phantastic, by which men see and gaze upon the cause of meteors: and by this vision, man discerns the Angels or <term>daemons</term> themselves as the causes of meteors. In this sort of inspection, man sometimes errs—namely by looking toward the created nature or the human spirit (which has the closest proximity to corporeal things)—for in attributing the efficient cause of the meteor to a created thing, he errs and seems to fall into the crime of Idolatry. But if he looks toward the internal part of the Angel, which is the light or divine emanation which it received immediately from the source <term>Ensoph</term> <note>The "Ein Sof" (Hebrew: "The Infinite"), the unknowable divine origin in Kabbalistic thought.</note>, to that extent he is not deceived in his vision, as it is intellectual. Finally, if we look back at the celestial bodies through the corporeal vision of the first order along with the Astrologers, or at the bodies of the elements and elemental things of the first degree with the <term>Peripatetic Philosophers</term> <note>Followers of Aristotle, who focused primarily on physical and material causes.</note>, it is necessary that we fall into great error and immerse ourselves in a deep sea of Idolatry, namely...

...namely, by attributing that admirable work to gross creatures, visible to the senses, which are in truth dead in themselves and of no importance—namely the sun, the other stars, the elements of fire and air, the heat of the earth, the cold of the middle region of the air, exhalations, vapors, and so on. Therefore, I advise all who are curious about philosophy that they should attribute the work and act of such great and miraculous procreation—and consequently the honor and glory—not to the elements or things made of elements, nor to the stars, nor even to the Angels (insofar as they are considered mere creatures), but to God the Creator alone. For it is He who produces all these things, and indeed far greater things in the world, in and through the angelic creatures. These angels are in the closest state of proximity and nearness to the Divinity, insofar as they immediately receive the impressions of light or divine emanations, which they then, moved by divine command, long to impart to creatures—both the perfect and the imperfectly mixed alike. 

Let me place before your considerations a most fitting comparison for this matter. A certain man wounds another with a sword: it is then asked, "Which of these men committed the wounding?" One person answers (after the manner of the <term>Peripatetics</term><note>The followers of Aristotle, who focused on physical, material causes.</note> who attribute the efficient cause of <term>meteors</term><note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon like wind, rain, or rainbows, not just falling stars.</note> to fire or air) that "the sword did this." But another (following the <term>Astrologers</term>, who attribute the acting cause to the stars or planets) will say that "the hand of the striker" is the doer of that deed. A third, coming closer to the truth (along with the <term>Magi</term> who say that the authors of meteors are <term>daemons</term><note>original: "dæmones." In this context, Fludd means "spirits" or "guiding intelligences," not necessarily evil beings.</note>), will say it is the "spirit within the man" that did it. Finally, one skilled in the <term>theographic mysteries</term><note>The study of how God writes His will into the world.</note>, looking with eyes somewhat sharper all the way to the center of each thing, will say that God did both this and that. By this example, the error of the world is clearly explained. 

However, in this place, we shall make mention of the winds only in the common manner, under which name we nevertheless understand the Angels of GOD, who are accustomed to animate them. But since we intend to act in a physical manner in this booklet of the third "member" and concern ourselves with the elements, we shall therefore treat the winds in this place after the manner of the common philosophers.

**CHAPTER II.**

*On the correct division of the winds, and that they are the efficient causes (speaking in the common tongue or after the common manner of philosophy) of every meteor, whether in the Air, Water, or Earth.*

We categorize winds (whose souls we have previously said are angels, either openly and manifestly or occultly bright) as either invisible and subject only to the sense of hearing, or visible and bright. Of the latter kind are lightnings, fire-whirls, flashes, and similar visible meteors which are driven through the air by violent motion, no differently than those winds that are visible. From these kinds of winds, then, as if from the prime movers in the elementary world, all other meteors are produced and procreated, whether bright or dark. These include: Comets, <term>chasms</term><note>original: "chasmata," referring to openings or "gaps" in the sky, often used to describe the Aurora Borealis.</note>, <term>beams</term><note>original: "trabes," another term for atmospheric light pillars.</note>, lightnings, flashes, <term>prester</term><note>A burning whirlwind or waterspout.</note>, "leaping goats," <term>will-o'-the-wisps</term><note>original: "ignis fatuus."</note>, and sulfurous flames which the earth vomits up. These come from visible winds which are clearly fiery, but which in their own nature are nothing but the most subtle air, animated and stirred up by a fiery soul. But truly, clouds, mists, vapors, snow, hail, stones, hoarfrost, and ice are created by hidden and less manifest winds—as if by efficient causes—and by hidden, dark air contracted into such dark forms. We shall now say a few words about these hidden and less visible winds, and we shall do so in the common manner.

**CHAPTER III.**

*On the East Wind [Subsolanus] and its two collateral winds.*

The hidden wind blowing directly from that place in the east where the equinoctial line intersects the Eastern horizon is called <term>Subsolanus</term><note>original: "Subsolanus," meaning "Below the Sun." The traditional Latin name for the East Wind.</note>, as it arises "under the Sun" in the Torrid Zone—specifically in that direct spot where the equator passes. Furthermore, it is called <term>Apeliotes</term> by the Greeks <note>original: "Apeliotes," meaning "from the sun."</note>. This wind, along with its two other collateral winds, is said to be hot and dry. But this wind—being the Prince of the eastern winds between the two aforementioned—stands like a Virtue in the middle; it is most temperate in its fiery disposition, like the celestial sun, which is why it is a bringer of clear skies to the Macrocosm <note>The Great World/Universe.</note> and is healthy for the Microcosm <note>The Little World/Man.</note>. 

Its right wing, which blows from that point of the eastern horizon where the Tropic of Cancer intersects—that is, from the summer sunrise—is called <term>Caecias</term> for its malice, and <term>Hellesponticus</term> after the place from which it blows. This wind is very inconstant in its disposition: for it is sometimes cold, following the nature of the North, and sometimes burning, following the nature of the East. For the most part, however, it exceeds all other winds in dryness, due to the nature of its location, insofar as it partakes of Northern or earthly dryness, and that of the East or...
                                                                                                                                                            fire.

<note>original: "Cæcias"</note> The Northeast wind partakes in the nature of fire. However, by accident, it is also sometimes observed to be imbued with a certain moisture. The left wing, or the collateral wind of the East wind <note>original: "subsolani collateralis"</note> towards the south, which blows from that point where the Tropic of Capricorn intersects the eastern horizon—that is, from the winter sunrise—is called *Eurus* in Greek, and is also called *Vulturnus* by some. Thus, it is sometimes—indeed, quite often—observed to gather clouds; yet, in respect to its dryness and heat, it is also sometimes observed to dissipate gathered clouds through the air, and to fill it everywhere with smoky mists and thick vapors. For this reason, it is known to deceive the sight, making visible objects appear larger than they truly are.

For a fuller explanation of the qualities of these winds, I refer and remit you to the following volume which, with God's favor, will deal with the nature of health and diseases.

## CHAPTER IV.

### Regarding the description of the West wind with its wings or collateral winds, and regarding the meteors <note>In this period, "meteors" refers to any atmospheric phenomenon like wind, rain, or snow.</note> which they are accustomed to produce in the air.

That general wind blowing from the corner of the west, whose midpoint is intersected by the equinoctial line, is called *Favonius* in Latin and *Zephyrus* in Greek—that is, "bearing life and vigor." This is the prince of those winds that blow from the west. In its nature, this wind is cold and moist in a most temperate degree. It has the *Africus* <note>The Southwest wind</note> to its right as its wing or collateral wind, and the *Corus* <note>The Northwest wind</note> to its left.

Therefore, the collateral wind *Africus* is that which blows from that point of the western horizon which is intersected by the Tropic of Capricorn—namely, from the winter solstice. Its disposition is to incline somewhat toward Southern heat, but Western coldness chiefly abounds in it. This wind is accustomed to blow impetuously in turns, which is why it is stormy and sometimes accompanied by clouds.

The other wing of the West wind, turning toward the North, is that wind which blows from that point in the west which the Tropic of Cancer intersects—namely, from the summer solstice. This is called *Corus* in Latin and *Argestes* in Greek—that is, "impetuous and stormy." In its condition, it inclines somewhat from the moisture of the West wind toward the dryness of the North. From this, it happens that it is naturally prone to hail, snow, and cold, and is moist in turns. While it blows, the clouds in the sky are observed to be dark, although for part of the day it may be serene, dry, and finally moist. Furthermore, because of its more intense moisture, it sometimes brings hail-filled rains and snows; in the summer, it quite frequently brings very violent thunder, lightning, and horrendous storms.

Concerning the production of these qualities—whether relating to disease or to health in both the macrocosm and microcosm—we shall speak copiously in the following volume, with God's assistance.

The North wind, called *Boreas* in Greek, is the principal wind of the North, and it is accustomed to blow directly from the Pole Star. In its condition, it is exceedingly cold and dry. This usually happens when a louder noise is heard; then it condenses the air into clouds, and sometimes, especially in the summer time, it is observed to produce thunder.

Its left wing is called *Aquilo* <note>The North-Northeast wind</note>, which blows from that point of the eastern region where the polar or arctic circle intersects the horizon. This wind, in its condition, is very cold and dry, but truly somewhat... <note>Text cuts off at "aliquantu-"</note>

## CHAPTER II.

# 288 Universal Experiment

**L. M.** is the neck of the matrass <term>matrass: a round-bottomed glass flask with a long neck, used in alchemy and early chemistry</term> whose opening is submerged in water.
**N.** is the hole in the cover through which the submerged part of the neck enters.
**M.** is the portion of the matrass neck divided into twelve equal parts.
**O.** is the body of the matrass, held upright.

We believe it is worthwhile to proceed quickly to the properties and use of this device. First, it must be observed that when the body of the matrass **O.** is heated, the air contained within it is thinned <note>original: "subtiliatur"</note> by the external heat. Once thinned, it requires a larger space to contain its existence. Thus, the greater portion of air—which had been gathered and contracted in the hollow of that body by the cold—now, being more or less thinned and dilated by the heat, requires a wider place for its existence. For this reason, a portion of it is forced to exit into the open air while the vessel or body of the matrass is heating up.

From this, it follows that when the opening of the matrass neck is placed into water (while the vessel is still warm), the more that body gradually cools, the more the water is drawn up into the neck of the matrass, specifically from degree 1 to 2, and then from 2 to 3. The reason for this is that the action of cold is in every way the opposite of heat. Therefore, if it is the nature of heat to thin things out and require a larger or more spacious place for the substance it has thinned or attenuated, it follows conversely that it is the nature of cold to thicken and gather the substance that was dispersed and rarefied by the heat, reducing it into a narrower space.

Consequently, as the vigor of the heat gradually fades and the power of the cold increases, a large portion of the air has already been expelled from the vessel's cavity by the previous thinning. Because of the barrier of the water, new air sufficient to match the growing spirit <note>Here, "spirit" refers to the air or gaseous substance within the glass</note> cannot be drawn into the belly of the vessel. Therefore, it is necessary for a portion of water to supply the "defect" <note>lack or absence</note> of air, being raised into the neck of the matrass in place of the air. This is because the thinned air that once filled the entire cavity of the body is now contracted into a narrower space by the restrictive and congealing faculty of the cold; without the water filling that space, it would leave a vacuum in the vessel, which Nature in no way permits—as has been discussed more extensively elsewhere.

Once the body of water has been drawn up and raised in this way due to the successive creeping in and abundance of cold, it becomes necessary that every subsequent increase in cold or heat can be discerned with the naked eye. For if either the air surrounding the vessel or something more physical placed against or adhering to the vessel grows warm—and the more intense the heat of that surrounding air or the object applied to the vessel becomes—the water will decline further downward toward the container <note>original: "pixidem," likely the water reservoir at the bottom</note>. For example, if the water stood at degree 6 or 7 during a state of cold, then upon an increase of heat in the surrounding air or by applying a hand or another object to the body, the water will descend by as many degrees as the proportion of heat has increased in the enclosed air.

The reason for this is readily apparent: as we have said, the greater the proportion of heat, the greater the thinning or rarefaction of the enclosed air. And the thinner a substance becomes, the more it seeks a wider and more free place for its existence. For a single handful of water dilated into air requires ten times as much space to be contained as it claimed for itself in its watery consistency. The same ratio or proportion exists between air and fire, for air ignited by heat migrates gradually into the thinness of fire.

It is for this reason that the air enclosed in the body of the vessel—previously contracted and reduced to a narrower space by cold—now, dilated by the approach of heat, thrusts the water that was raised in the neck downward, so that it might acquire a larger or smaller space for itself according to the degree of its rarefaction. Are we not taught by experience that water reduced to vapor by the violence of fire requires a much vaster space for its freedom? Whoever wishes to equip themselves more exactly for the investigation of this matter, we refer them to the experiments brought forth by us in Chapter 2, Experiments 12, 13, and 16; Tractate 2, Part 7, Book 3, Chapter 1, Rules 6 and 7. There we have clearly expressed the infinite faculty of Nature dilating itself.

Furthermore, this is explained even more clearly to the uninitiated by the example of gunpowder. A small portion of it in its earthy substance is usually converted into a great smoke like a massive cloud, snatching and shattering everything in its path if its spacious freedom is impeded. Likewise, in the extraction of "strong water" <note>original: "aquae fortis," or nitric acid</note> distilled from saltpeter and vitriol, we find that the receiving vessel must contain the massive spirits leaping out from the mouth of the retort.

We conclude, therefore, that heat, by dilating, causes the air enclosed in the body to repel the water raised in the neck, so that the dilated air may acquire a larger space for itself, according to the greater or lesser dominance of the heat’s effect on the enclosed air.

But truly, as the effect of heat decreases and fades, and cold gradually revives and predominates, it is necessary that the power and operation of the preceding heat be removed, and that the property and act of cold—which is contrary to heat—be produced. Thus, just as the water raised in the neck was pushed downward by the action of heat, so now a contrary effect is produced by the contrary affection of cold.

The reason for this matter is as follows: just as it is the property of heat to thin and rarefy (in which act a wider space is required to contain the thinned substance), so too...
