In this way, indeed, it is the duty of the cold’s domain to thicken and make dense that which heat has thinned <note>original: "subtiliauit"; referring to the process of rarefaction where a substance becomes less dense</note>. In this capacity, cold contracts into a smaller space and quantity that which heat has dilated. The more the effects of cold assault the air, the more the air is constricted and compressed into a narrower space.

From this, therefore—lest a vacuum be created <note>The Aristotelian principle of "horror vacui," the idea that nature will do anything to prevent an empty space</note>—it follows that the same water which the action of heat pushed downward is pulled upward by the action of cold as it contracts the air. The water is carried upward by as many degrees as the cold is exalted in its dominance over the power of heat.

As for the initial reasoning behind these properties, it has been explained by us at length in Book 1, Chapter 4 of the first part of this work, where the accidental principles of meteors <note>In the 17th century, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and clouds, not just falling stars</note> are discussed; we shall also explain the same more clearly in the following sections.

### CHAPTER III.

### On the various uses of this experimental instrument.

Although the primary goal in demonstrating such an instrument is to derive a most suitable observation of meteors from its dual and contrary motions, it is nevertheless my intention here to speak briefly—and not irrelevantly to our subsequent contemplation—of its common uses.

By its general constructive action (that is, the rising of water through the contraction of air), we perceive the logic of **Density** or the thickness of any thing; this action of nature proceeds from cold, as you have heard above. Conversely, by the mediating action of dilation (by which the water is pushed downward due to the dissipation and resolution of the enclosed air), we perceive the cause of the **Rare** or of subtlety in nature, a property derived from heat. From this, it is certain—and we are made more sure beyond all doubt—that nothing in the universal kingdom of nature can be rarefied or thinned except by the mediation of light or fire (whether it be visible or invisible), the effect of which is heat. Likewise, nothing can be condensed, constricted, or thickened where darkness does not hold dominion, as the effect of darkness is cold, just as was clearly explained in the place cited previously.

Its more specific uses are manifold. First, and most evidently, it is accustomed to indicate the natural state and temperament of the external air in terms of heat and cold. For the higher the water reaches through the degrees of the neck <note>The long neck of the glass flask</note>, the greater is the dominion of cold in the air. Thus, in any quarter of the year, or even any day of the week, we can judge the degrees of cold by the rising of the water. Indeed, even within the same day, we may perceive the conflict between the solar heat and the cold, along with many other things worthy of observation. Furthermore, by the same logic, through the contrary motion, we may determine the dominance of heat in any quarter, day, or hour of the year. These observations are matters of no small importance in the uncovering of nature and her mysteries.

Moreover, these same effects are usually produced by "accidental" <note>External or temporary</note> heat or cold. Thus, if we simply apply a hand to the bottom of the glass vessel <note>original: "matracei"; a matrass is a round-bottomed flask with a long neck</note>, the enclosed air, thinned by the heat of the applied limb, forces the water to incline downward in the blink of an eye. When the hand is removed from the vessel, the water immediately seeks to breathe back into its original place assigned to it by natural cold.

Finally, by proper observation of such an instrument and vigilant attention to the movement of the water, we can measure the heat of chemical furnaces. If we have two such instruments at hand—one exposed to the mildness of the naturally affected air, and the other applied to a vent breathing from the furnace—they will provide a ratio for adapting the artificial heat of the one to the natural heat of the other. Thus, the one applied to the artificial heat will be "rectified" <note>Adjusted or calibrated</note> in its degree by the natural one. From this, it will be very easy to derive a unity of proportion in artificial heat in this manner: by adapting the degree of heat in the natural air to the artificial one. For example, if the instrument disposed to the natural air has pushed the water back only to the 7th degree, but the heat of the instrument applied to the furnace has depressed it to the 4th degree, then I may observe that the artificial fire exceeds the natural fire by only three degrees. Therefore, if the natural heat in the air decreases in the future and the water rises to the 8th or 9th degree, I shall wait until the water in the artificially applied instrument rises by the same proportion to the 5th or 6th degree. In this way, it always maintains a triple proportion in its distance <note>A constant difference of three degrees</note>, which is to be ascribed to the artificial heat; and so it is for all other cases.

Now I shall proceed to the second part of this book, where, God willing, we shall discuss the strict contemplation of the generation of meteors, having taken into account the action and properties of this spiritual instrument <note>original: "instrumenti istius spiritalis"; 'spiritual' here refers to the 'spiritus' or air/breath contained within the device</note>.

# On Manna

Both the Pagans and the Christians well-versed in pagan philosophy have admitted that the substance of manna is a certain honey-like dew descending from the sky. However, they also affirm that the origin of this same dew (vainly nourishing their own fantasies with imaginary willpower) comes from the earth and water—specifically from a very fatty and viscous vapor. They claim it arises from a mixture of water and earth as soon as the air is exhaled from the interior elements, which then falls back upon plants through congealing, like sugar or a very sweet flour. In this opinion, they always seem to establish the foundations and bases of their philosophy on an erroneous footing, deriving visible things from visible things rather than from the invisible. Yet the reality of the matter, according to the testimony of Holy Scripture, is quite different. We are taught there (as has been frequently cited before) that it must be believed through faith that visible things were previously made from those things which are invisible. <note>The author is referencing Hebrews 11:3: "Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear."</note> We say, therefore, that Manna is a dense type of **Meteor**, <term>Meteor: in the 17th century, this referred to any atmospheric phenomenon like rain, snow, or dew, not just falling stars.</term> produced by the thickening of the celestial air when it is soaked with moisture. *Does not,* says a certain eminent philosopher, *I pray you, consider a simple cloud of water: Who would ever believe that it contains within itself all things that the world has—hard stones, salts, air, earth, fire—and yet by itself it appears to be simple water?* Thus he spoke. But indeed, in the places previously cited, we have proved clearly enough by reasons established in the Holy Bible that vapors, clouds, and their waters are formed from the condensation of simple air and brought forth into the world.

We, therefore, have deemed it fit to describe Manna in this manner, according to the laws of holy testimony:
Manna is a fatty substance of the air which, when the gates of heaven are opened and the divine treasury is unlocked, descends from the clouds by divine command in the manner of dew or frost. It appears in a minute form, round like white coriander seed, growing as it falls upon the lands to carry out the will of the Creator.

Or like this:
Manna is celestial bread, the wheat of heaven, spiritual meat, the food of angels, and the very word proceeding from the mouth of Jehovah. It descends by divine power from the sky and the clouds in the manner of a dewy rain—either together with the celestial dew or upon the dew—onto the surface of the earth. It takes a minute and round form, similar to humped frost or coriander seed, congealing there into hardness so that it might serve as food, nourishment, and even medicine for men.

In our first description, you have the **material cause** <note>The author is using Aristotelian logic, which explains an object through four "causes": what it's made of (material), its shape (formal), who made it (efficient), and its purpose (final).</note> of Manna expressed, insofar as it is described there as being a "fatty substance of the air." Next, the **formal cause** is expressed in that it is said to "grow into a minute species and round like coriander seed." Then, afterward, we declared its **efficient cause** to be the "divine command"—that is, the Power and the Word. Finally, we affirm the **final cause** (the occasion of its descent or generation) is "to carry out the will of the Creator." You have all these parts of our description confirmed specifically from the pages of Holy Scripture in this way:

For regarding the **material cause**, *God said to the Israelites, "Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you" (Exodus 16:4).* And elsewhere, *“He gave them celestial bread to eat” (John 6:31).* And elsewhere, *“He had commanded the clouds from above and opened the doors of heaven, and rained down Manna upon them.”* By which it is declared clearly enough that the matter of Manna itself is of an aerial composition, since by the word "heaven," the air is understood, as it is the place of the clouds which Jehovah commanded. Hence the treasury-chest of Manna, in which it is reserved and from which it is fashioned as to its substance, is the air itself. 

The **form** is also explained by these words: *“And in the morning, the dew lay round about the host... and behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground” (Exodus 16:14).* And elsewhere: *“Manna was like white coriander seed, and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.”* And elsewhere: *“Its taste was like the taste of the most excellent moisture of oil” (Numbers 11:7).* 

Furthermore, the **efficient** or creating **cause** is confirmed by these words: *“I (says Jehovah) rain bread from heaven for you” (Exodus 16:4).* And elsewhere: *“He had commanded the clouds from above and opened the doors of heaven, and rained down Manna upon them.”* 

Finally, the **end** (purpose) of this kind of meteor is explained where it is said: *“He fed thee with Manna... that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word, etc.” (Deuteronomy 8:3).* And elsewhere: *“Thou feddest thine own people with angels' food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labor, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste” (Wisdom 16:20).* And elsewhere: *“He gave them celestial bread to eat” (John 6:31).*

We conclude, therefore, that in addition to all this, you have the place of generation for this kind of divine nourishment in our said description: namely, that it descends from the clouds when the gates of heaven are opened and the divine treasury is unlocked. For it is written, *“Behold, I rain bread from heaven for you” (Exodus 16).* And elsewhere: *“He had commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, and rained down Manna upon them” (Psalm 78:24-25).* <note>The original text cites Psalm 78:25, but the quote typically refers to the "bread of the mighty" or "angels' food" found in verses 24-25.</note>

In the second description as well, you have the four causes of this kind of meteor exactly explained. But the **material cause** is explained in a more abstruse manner: as bread and wheat of heaven, as spiritual meat, the food of angels, and indeed even as the "material Word"—the **efficient cause** of which we make Jehovah himself. The place from which it is drawn is the sky and the clouds. The method of its emanation is indicated, along with the **formal cause**: namely, that it descends to the surface of the earth in the manner of a dewy rain, or together with celestial dew, or upon the dew, congealing into hardness in a minute and round form, similar to humped frost or coriander seed. Finally, its **final cause** is explained in that it serves men as both food and nourishment, as well as medicine.

It is understood that salts, stones, flesh, blood, and everything that can be found in the world originally arise from thin water. But indeed, we have maintained that the cloud itself arises from the air or the heavens and not from the earth, which is also confirmed by the divine writings: *The Lord shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven, to give the rain unto thy land in his season.* <note>original: *Aperiet tibi Iehoua theſaurum ſuum optimum cœlos, dando pluuiam terræ tuæ tempore ſuo, Ex. 28. 12.* This is likely a reference to Deuteronomy 28:12, though the text cites Exodus.</note> He did not say He will open the lands, but the heaven—that is, the air—as if he had said: the Lord will open the womb or the hidden matrix of the air, making the hidden things of the air manifest. The Apostle <note>Referring to St. Paul.</note> also teaches us in the place cited above that all visible things were previously invisible. From this it is clear that not only visible water, but even the earth, and consequently stone (which is the denser portion of water), comes from the invisible spirit, which is spiritual water. Regarding their formal cause <term>Formal cause: A philosophical term referring to the design, shape, or essence that makes a thing what it is.</term>, I will say nothing in this place, as it is known to almost anyone through visual experience.

However, we say that the "efficient cause" <term>Efficient cause: The agent or force that brings something into being; the "actor" behind an event.</term> proposed by others is erroneous and most false, as it is opposed to the Holy Scriptures. They claim that the heat of the Sun and the stars brought this meteor <term>Meteor: In the 17th century, this referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, or lightning, not just falling space rocks.</term> to perfection. Yet the Holy Bible assigns this work not to the creatures, but immediately to the Creator. Although He has placed His tabernacle in the sun, He does not dwell there exclusively; rather, He dwells everywhere by His presence, fills all things, and acts everywhere according to His will. For He Himself, who is the eternal fountain of light, is consequently the origin of action, motion, and heat, both in the stars and in the entire world. Hence St. John says in *Chapter 1: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made; in him was life,* <note>original: *Ab eo omnia ſunt facta, & ſine eo nihil, in eo erat vita.*</note> and elsewhere: *The incorruptible Spirit of God is in every thing.* <note>original: *Spiritus DEI incorruptibilis eſt in omni re. Sap. 12.* Referring to the Wisdom of Solomon 12:1.</note> We say, therefore, that the Lord God is both the mediate and the immediate efficient cause of a matter of such great importance. He is the *Alpha and Omega,* between whose prior and posterior acts there is no distinction or separation in essence, because just as He is permanent in Himself, so also are His actions permanent.

But (my good Peripatetics) <note>Peripatetics: Followers of Aristotle’s philosophy, who often focused on naturalistic explanations rather than direct divine intervention.</note> if it were true that the influence of the heavens or the stars were the authors of such fiery meteors, I would very much like to know whether there was thunder in the world before the creation of the heavenly host or not? And yet, we can very easily gather from the sense of the Holy Scriptures that God spoke through thunder even at the beginning of the world's creation, through the passages to be cited by us a little further down where mention of thunder will be made; from which it follows that such an opinion is not well-founded. And although it has been proven by the more skilled Astrologers taught by experience that thunder is heard after certain aspects <term>Aspects: The relative positions and angles between planets that astrologers believe influence earthly events.</term> of certain planets, it does not follow that this happens by necessity. We observe that such effects do not always follow such planetary aspects. For it is in God's power—to whom alone it is given to act according to His will—to act sometimes through His planetary instruments (directing His face from His solar tabernacle toward this or that planet, or many at once), sometimes by means of His winds (who must obey their Commander), and we observe this happening quite often with no obvious celestial cause preceding it. Sometimes it is performed by fiery or watery spirits and demons carrying out the Creator’s commands, and in infinite other hidden ways which would be impossible for even the most skilled Astrologer to explore. How and by what means God works to produce meteors in the world, we have proposed to speak clearly below, where the natural efficient cause is treated.

Finally, regarding what a "lightning stone" <note>original: *lapis fulminaris*. Similarly elsewhere: *Lord, bow thy heavens and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke. # CHAPTER XIII.
# On the Luminous Meteors of Both Worlds.

**Luminous Meteors of the Macrocosm** <term>Meteors: In the 17th century, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon (wind, rain, lightning, etc.), not just falling space rocks.</term> are either:

*   **Angelic spirit or fiery animating wind**, which is fiery and luminous:
    *   Not appearing, but lurking in the air in a secret way.
    *   Appearing and visibly, and is either:
        *   Shimmering,
        *   Flashing,
        *   Lightning-flashing,
        *   Striking with thunderbolts,
        *   **OR**
        *   Of a superior and thinner substance, such as:
            *   **Comets of various forms** (discussed below),
            *   **Column of fire**,
            *   **Beam**,
            *   **Spear**,
            *   **Flying sparks**.
        *   Of a middle substance, such as thunder mixed with lightning, and *chasmata* <term>Chasmata: A term for atmospheric "gaps" or "chasms" appearing in the night sky, often associated with the Aurora Borealis.</term>.

*   **Manifest and visible things**, for whose composition two things concur:
    *   **An animated airy body**, that is, one illustrated by light or fire, and is of either:
        *   The evening redness of the sky.
        *   Radiations or *Affub* <note>original: "Affub"; an Arabic-derived term used in medieval science for shooting stars or sudden atmospheric lights.</note> quickly appearing and disappearing.
        *   Airy things mixed with light or fire, such as:
            *   **Falling stars**,
            *   **Will-o'-the-wisp** <note>original: "Ignis fatuus."</note>,
            *   **Hair-licking fire** <note>original: "ignis crines lambens"; likely referring to static electricity or St. Elmo's fire appearing around people or objects.</note>,
            *   **Castor and Pollux** <term>Castor and Pollux: The traditional name for the twin glows of St. Elmo’s fire seen on ships' masts during storms.</term>, etc.
    *   **Of an inferior and more coarse substance**, tending toward "burnt melancholy" <note>In the humoral theory of the time, "burnt melancholy" (melancholia adusta) referred to a heavy, dry, and dark elemental state.</note>, and are either:
        *   **Coarser**, of a sulfurous or bituminous nature.
        *   **Thinner**, and of this kind is the yellow and red earth [vapors].

*   **Hidden things**: See Book L.

The matter of Comets, therefore, is a denser part of its own sphere—namely, the fiery sphere—coagulated into one by the opposing

proceed from the element of fire or the supreme region of the air, because that portion of the air is too thin to

vaporous substance from which clouds are usually formed, and consequently the crashes of thunder cannot be produced in that place 
due to the lack of watery moisture there, which ought to resist the impulse of the fiery spirits.

sometimes found there, though rarely; these are not as massive as the bulk of clouds, since the 
thinness of the region’s consistency cannot produce such a mass in its condensation. Furthermore, the winds 
are not forceful in that region—indeed, they are scarcely sensible—since they find 
little or no resistance there, due to the thinness and dryness of the region's consistency. And this is especially 
to be considered: that fiery spirits always mix themselves with the substance of their own nature and illuminate it, in the manner 
of that royal spirit who set his tabernacle in the sun; which bright spirits indeed receive

solar tabernacle, from which the bright force of life is not only flashed forth to the stars and every other bright creature on all sides,

their own proper spheres, from which these lights are then afterwards imparted to and showered upon the elements—
lights which the elementary demons receive and drink in, and according to the divine will, pour out either visibly 
or invisibly into the elements; which outpourings indeed include light, motion, and those Aristotelian 
influences. These things having been considered, we descend thus to a general description of comets and of whatever 
fiery impressions:

A Comet or <term>Assub</term> <note>An Arabic-derived term for a meteor or falling star.</note> of the superior order is an aerial body, gathered and condensed in the upper region of the same 
by angelic breath, animated and inspired by a bright spirit through the rays of divine wisdom acting through its 
angelic ministers, ordained by the most holy name of the said wisdom for the fulfillment of the will 
of the Father or Creator here on the earth, in the waters, and in the air, and finally, after dissolution 
has occurred, invisibly expanded through the common air.

In which description of a fiery impression of the superior order, its material cause

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors. 113

For in truth, the meteors of the upper region of the air, as far as their bodies are concerned, are nothing other than spiritual clouds, which do not dissolve into rain like the lower clouds, but finally vanish into the air in the manner of "spirit of wine" <note>original: "spiritus vini," referring to highly distilled alcohol or ethanol</note> that has been many times rectified; though it is visible in its mass, once the glass is opened it vanishes invisibly into the air and is gradually resolved. Thus we see that the clouds in the higher part of the middle region, which are saffron-colored, never dissolve into rain, but are accustomed to return and be transmuted into subtle and invisible air, from which they were originally derived; hence they are called dry and sterile clouds. In exactly the same way, the air in the highest region—placed and gathered there by the power of "ignited demons" <note>In this context, "demons" refers to spiritual beings or intelligences, not necessarily evil spirits</note>—is sometimes reduced into such clouds, though they differ far from the others in their brightness and purity. Secondly, we have expressed the **formal cause** <term>formal cause: the essential nature or "blueprint" of a thing that makes it what it is</term> of the same in a general way there: namely, that it is a visible aerial body, animated and inspired by a lucid and flashing spirit. Thirdly, we have made the **efficient and informing cause** <term>efficient cause: the agent or force that brings something into being</term> twofold: namely, the **primary**, which is Wisdom herself, and the **secondary or assistant**, which are the angelic ministers whom we also call "demons." Furthermore, it is written, *Who made the sapphire clouds by wisdom? By such a fiery scourge seventy thousand men of the Israelites died invisibly, with the Angel of GOD striking and smiting them, *2 Samuel 24:16.* So also we see that the substance of a comet, invisibly dissipated through the air, frequently produces plagues, famine, and dryness of the earth, as is declared by the effect. But I would have you understand that there are undoubtedly very many Comets and other fiery impressions in the air which are entirely invisible to men, both in their rising and their effect, which are beyond all controversy the causes of various epidemic diseases, as is discussed more copiously in the chapter *On the invisible bright meteor.* We say, therefore, that GOD, through the mediation of His flaming angelic ministers (among whom we recognize Wisdom as the chief and primary), is the efficient cause not only of every fiery Meteor but also of the aqueous ones and every other kind. And although the Peripatetics and many others ascribe such a duty to the stars, the element of fire, and the coldness of the middle region of the air, yet it is the part of a true Christian to attribute such acts to the [First] Act—namely, to give to God what is of God, and by no means to arrogantly claim them for created things. Because of a lack of such consideration, so great a perversity of Idolatry arose among the Heathens, and the neglect of the true worship of God; to this error it must be attributed that almost every nation of Barbarians set about to fashion and establish a new God for itself.

Others maintain that lightning bolts arise from hot and dry winds, trapped by clouds that are tightly compressed and enclosed. Finally, this kind of natural operation is so marvelous that some individuals—immersing themselves more deeply into the mysteries of God and nature and diligently considering the admirable power and operation of the lightning bolt—have judged it to be not a work of nature, but the highest immediate effect of God. Every true Christian ought to be counted among their number. But first, we shall hasten to the examination of that Aristotelian definition.

# On the Formal Cause of Atmospheric Phenomena. 117

<note>The "formal cause" refers to the essential nature or "voice" of the phenomenon, according to Aristotelian philosophy.</note> 

...before the brightness in his sight the clouds passed, and the Lord thundered from heaven etc. <note>original: *præfulgore in conspectu eius nubes transierunt, & intonuit de cælo dominus*</note> Psalm 17. <note>In modern Bibles, this is Psalm 18.</note> Finally, the purpose of thunder and lightning is declared there: namely, that it is as much for judging the people as for giving food in abundance.

->Or thus.<-

**Thunder** is the voice of the Most High, mixed with flame and lightning, sent and ordained by God to disturb the wicked. In this form, the "crash" or "voice" is the **formal cause**, while the **efficient cause** is Jehovah himself, and the **end** <note>The "final cause" or purpose.</note> is as a scourge for the wicked.

This is confirmed in the preceding passage: The Lord thundered (says the Royal Psalmist) from heaven, the Most High gave his voice, hail and coals of fire, and he sent out his arrows, and scattered them; he multiplied lightnings and discomfited them. Psalm 17.

->Or thus:<-

**Thunder** is the voice or sound proceeding from the throne of God via lightning, sent forth from the cavity of a cloud into the open air by the divine power, according to His will, for either evil or good, to be executed both in the heavens and on the earth.

Where the **formal cause** is the voice or sound, the **efficient cause** is the lightning of God, and the **end** is either for a blessing or a curse.

It is confirmed thus: In the Apocalypse it is written, *From the throne proceed lightnings*, Revelation 4:5. And elsewhere: *Will you send lightnings and they will go, and returning say, "Here we are"?* Job 38:35. And elsewhere: *Smoke ascended in his anger, and fire from his face glowed, etc.* Psalm 17. And elsewhere: *Clouds and darkness are round about him, fire proceeds before him, and shall inflame his enemies round about; his lightnings shone upon the world, etc.* Psalm 97:2. And elsewhere: *The clouds gave a voice, for your arrows passed through, etc.* Psalm 76. <note>Psalm 77 in modern numbering.</note> Where by "arrows" in this place, he seems to mean lightnings. Whence it is also written elsewhere: *The shafts of lightnings shall go directly, and as from a well-curved bow of clouds they shall be ejected,* Wisdom 5:21. From which he seems to imply that the clouds "gave a voice" because the lightnings passed through and penetrated them.

->Or thus:<-

**Thunder** is the voice of God raised in a cloud, surrounded and covered on all sides by the force of waters, before which a fire goes and inflames everything around Him.

Hence Job says: *Will you lift up your voice in a mist, and will the rush of waters cover you?* Job 38:34. And elsewhere: *Clouds and darkness are round about him, fire proceeds before him, and shall inflame his enemies round about.* Psalm 97:2.

->Or thus:<-

**Thunder** is the voice of God, at which he gives a multitude of waters in heaven, and makes lightnings and rain. Hence it is written: *At his voice he gives a multitude of waters in heaven, and lifts up the mists from the ends of the earth; he makes lightnings into rain, and brings forth the wind out of his treasures,* Jeremiah 10:13.

->Or thus:<-

**Thunder** is the multitude of the sound of waters, or the voice of the clouds, brought about by God’s flashes of lightning shining upon the whole world.

->Or thus:<-

**Thunder** is the sound of a multitude of waters, fearing and disturbed at the sight of Jehovah, or a voice or crash going around, which the clouds are accustomed to give; this voice is produced or procreated immediately by the flashes of lightning proceeding from the throne of God and breaking out from the clouds (which are the "tent" of Jehovah) to execute the divine will.

In this description, the **material organ** of such a voice is the waters, acting as if they are afraid and disturbed, whence they are accustomed to give out a voice, or sound, or crash, because of the penetrating power which the bright and shining sight of God, the worker of wonders, produces. Hence it is said: *Before the brightness in his sight the clouds passed, hail and coals of fire; the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice,* Psalm 17. And elsewhere: *The waters saw you, O GOD, and they were afraid, and the depths were troubled; a multitude of the sound of waters, the clouds gave a voice, the voice of your thunder was in the wheel.* Psalm 76:17.

The **formal cause** is also described in this: that it happens with a crash and with flashes of lightning.

The **efficient cause** seems to be the lightnings, or rather the fiery gaze of God animating the lightnings themselves and directing them to the goal ordained by God; wherefore lightnings are as it were the instruments of God in His wrath, just as a sword is the instrument of a man who strikes—where we say such a man struck with a sword, and not the sword itself. Therefore, we call God alone the actor in these things, the father of the thunders themselves, who sends out lightnings like His arrows from His throne, according to that passage in the Apocalypse.

Furthermore, we have placed the **end** <note>The purpose or final cause.</note> as being to fulfill the divine will.

->Or finally in this manner:<-

**Thunder** is the voice, or speech, or eloquence, or sound proceeding from the mouth of Jehovah, which is directed under the whole heaven with light over the ends or borders of the earth; after which a sound roars, or God thunders with the voice of His excellence, and it cannot be tracked down when His voice is heard, He who thundering performs wonderfully with His voice.

We have this confirmed by the words of Sacred Scripture in this way: *Listen with trembling to the voice or speech, or (as another interprets it) the eloquence proceeding from His mouth; He directs it under the whole heaven, that eloquence and...*

Therefore, against the foolish opinions of the Pagans <note>The author uses "Ethnicorum" to refer to non-Christian, classical Greek and Roman philosophers.</note>, it is demonstrated that neither exhalations nor vapors, nor the sun with the stars, nor earth or water, nor the elements, nor created nature itself, but God himself—who is the operator of all wonders—is the immediate efficient cause <term>efficient cause: the primary agent that brings something into being</term> of these marvels. We have this confirmed by Holy Scripture, so that we do not falsely attribute to nature, or its elements, or things made from elements, those things which are to be attributed first and before all else to the Creator; for in doing so, we might unexpectedly cast ourselves headlong into foul idolatry along with those Pagans.

But I know well that it will be objected by some that the kind of thunders spoken of in the Holy Scriptures were miraculous and not at all "natural." Both recent and ancient philosophers fall into this opinion: namely, that thunders are sometimes natural and sometimes supernatural. They act as if the things which occur in the moisture of the world's nature are not done immediately by God, just like those things which happen according to the season of the year or the hot intemperance of summer, or those in winter or for other hidden reasons. Yet it cannot be unknown to a true Christian that God is everywhere, and has his dwelling both in the elements themselves and in the things formed from elements. For in the highest heaven He is clothed in light as a garment; in the middle of heaven He placed His tabernacle in the Sun; and in the lowest region He made the thick cloud His hut. Indeed, as Job testifies: *Jehovah answered him out of the whirlwind.* <note>original: "Iehoua ei respondebat è turbine"</note> Furthermore, He is also on the earth. *For the earth shall bring forth the Savior.* He speaks in the Prophet and through the mouth of the Prophet; indeed, God uses every single thing of this world as His organ <term>organum: a tool or instrument used by an agent to produce an effect</term>, and He speaks in various ways according to the variety of the organ. In the simple worldly spirit His voice is neither heard nor understood, except by those who are enlightened or stirred by the spirit; He speaks in the angels and through the mediation of angelic organs; but to mortals, He most often speaks terribly in His wrath—that is, in thunder. Whence Job says: *Hear with trembling the voice going out of his mouth under the whole heaven and the light over the borders of the earth. Job 37.* Therefore, those philosophers are of unsound mind who distinguish thunders into "vain and brute"—those which seem to signify nothing—and "prophetic and significant." As if thunders should be called "vain and brute" just because God’s intention (who produced nothing in the world in vain) was not revealed to them in the moment of their creation! O how hidden are the mysteries of God, and how concealed from the knowledge of profane men!

Nor indeed can I praise Cicero’s skill in this matter, who in his book *On Divination* <note>original: "Lib. De Diuinat."</note> seems to deny that any kind of divination can arise from the observation of lightning, and does so quite thoughtlessly, making it out to be vain and empty. And yet we are taught the opposite by the Holy Bible, where it is written: *That God is great, surpassing our knowledge; He extends the clouds as His tent according to His pleasure, and He lightens with His light from above; He also covers the bottoms of the sea, for by these things He judges the peoples, and gives food to many mortals; in His hands He hides the light, and commands it to come again, etc. Job 36.* From these words it is right to gather that God lightens to execute justice upon mortals, and also converts lightning into rain for the benefit of mortals. Whence it is said elsewhere: *When He utters His voice, the waters in the heaven are multiplied; He lifts the clouds from the ends of the earth, He makes lightnings for the rain, and brings forth the winds out of His treasures. Jeremiah 51:15.* From this it is clear that there is no thunder unless it be the voice of Jehovah. Whence the Royal Psalmist speaks generally of thunder in these words: *The voice of Jehovah is upon the waters; the voice of the strong and glorious God thunders; the voice of Jehovah is upon many waters; the voice of Jehovah is powerful and in His strength; the voice of Jehovah is in majesty; the voice of Jehovah breaks the cedars, Jehovah even breaks the cedars of Lebanon, and makes them skip like a calf, Lebanon and Sirion; the voice of Jehovah divides the flames of fire; the voice of Jehovah shakes the desert; the voice of Jehovah makes the hinds to calve and strips the forests bare; but in His temple everyone speaks of His glory, etc. Psalm 29.* Here the King makes mention of the terrible voice of Jehovah, and of that peaceful one.

We conclude, therefore, that it is the greatest folly of any Christian—indeed, an unrecoverable madness—to place such faith in the vain and lying opinions of the Pagans who toss about empty words concerning thunder. These people try to persuade men that thunders and lightnings are merely accidental things, arising from the natural intemperance of the heavens and not at all sent by God. Thus, looking only at the effect, they eagerly take it falsely for the efficient cause. That is, they wish to attribute to creatures what belongs to God, the creator of every thing. Thus they proceed not only to babble thoughtlessly but to blaspheme impiously, leading men to idolatry, as if someone were to attribute the life of a man to his body and not to his soul. Therefore, I would have you know that I have written in this place not at all rashly, but diligently, supported by good foundations; other philosophers, deeper in the more abstruse mystery of Jehovah, seem to agree with me—those who, considering the wonderful operation of lightning, judged it not a work of nature, but an immediate effect of the most high God.

->On the Formal Cause of Atmospheric Phenomena. 119<-

...you think it is produced by a severe imbalance of the air. I would wish that you listen to this warning of ours, and not flippantly reject it or consider it as nothing, if we shall prove that lightning and thunder proceed immediately from God. For in this duty of mine, I shall provide not only comfort to you in your tribulation, but also glory and honor to God my creator.

Know then how the "wise" of this world—the followers of the pagan philosophers—rave, have raved, and will continue to rave in their obstinacy. Indeed, they do not concede that God works all things in all, and that His Word moves, stirs, and preserves all things. Instead, they ascribe these things to "created nature," pretending that God acts out of necessity through mediators—specifically through secondary and tertiary causes. <note>The author is criticizing the "Peripatetics" (followers of Aristotle) who believed God created the world but that nature now runs according to its own mechanical or biological laws, known as "secondary causes."</note> Thus wandering in error, they are unwilling to understand that God operates solely through His Word, and not through other "necessary" means; therefore, He works by no means through those causes alleged by them, but only through them as if they were instruments.

But you, who are nourished in the Holy Bible and governed by the law of Christ, I persuade you to conceive and forever turn over in your minds this: that God created the first substance—namely, water—as something moist or humid through His Word. This very substance even today, after the lapse of so many thousands of years, remains humid. Again, from this water, the heaven and the earth were created (as Saint Peter testifies) by means of the Word. Furthermore, in the heaven, He produced the light, the sun, the moon and stars, day and night, and all other created things by the command of His Word, and He imposed upon them their services. Because of this, all those things perform their duties according to that Word. Where, then, is the "nature" of the Peripatetics <note>Peripatetics: A term for followers of Aristotle, named after the walkways (peripatoi) in the Lyceum where he taught.</note> which is supposed to carry these things out? There is clearly nothing anywhere except the one and only Word of God, which works these and all other things, according to that saying of the Evangelist: *All things were made by the Word, and without it, nothing was made; in it was life,* etc. (John 1). From this it is clear that without Him, nothing can exist or act. Therefore, insofar as the air is part of the celestial substance, it follows that it was made by the Word, and "swims" as it were in the Word, as that which embraces all things and is moved and governed by the Word of God itself. Indeed, even in the air, as if in God's universal treasury chest, He has His peculiar storehouses <note>original: "areas"</note> from which various species of atmospheric phenomena <term>meteors: In early modern science, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, snow, wind, and rainbows, not just falling stars.</term> are produced. These He has placed under the protection and governance of various angels and spirits (who were also created from the air and in the air by the Word), just as it is right to gather from various places in the Holy Scriptures which we shall cite below. By their administration (the Word moving and operating), all atmospheric phenomena are produced in the air, and all storms which usually happen to the world arise in a wonderful way. Hence it is said, *He made his angels winds, and his ministers a burning flame,* etc. Thus, at the beginning of the world, God created the angels together with the air, so that they might perform and execute their duty and office regarding the direction of storms, rain, snow, hail, frost, clouds, lightning, thunder, fire, chasms <note>original: "chasmatum," likely referring to auroras or gaps in the clouds</note>, thunderbolts, waters, heat, cold, humidity, dryness, and many other things of that kind. This is indeed unknown to the pagan philosophers and their Christian followers, for a lying and false spirit has claimed a seat for itself in their mouths and writings. From this spirit, their ignorance and the vanity of their philosophy has arisen. This is no wonder, since they knew neither GOD nor His most holy Word; indeed, despising the Holy Scripture or reading it very little, but dwelling only on their own delusions, they are accustomed to sew lie upon lie. If those Christian disciples of the pagan Peripatetics had read through the Holy Bible with the same zeal with which they turned through the false Aristotelian books and volumes, they would have found the truth about the air and storms—that those things do not behave in the way those men wrote in their books filled with imaginations. Rather, God has His own peculiar treasury chests in the open air for these species already mentioned, from which He produces winds and storms; the air "swims" and consists in the Word of God, and is led by the angels appointed for this purpose, with the Word of God directing them, when, where, and how God wills. Thus, if ever dangerous storms arise, they can call upon God, that He might wish to mercifully turn away that danger of the storm, and in its place grant kind rain, and at the same time defend, protect, and preserve the fruits of the earth together with men and cattle from all evil; and so that they might also consider anything else regarding all these things which can yield to the honor of God. # On the Formal Cause of Meteors. 123

Those fiery meteors <note>original: "meteora," referring here to any atmospheric phenomena, not just falling stars</note> which are of a higher nature—that is, located in a more elevated place, namely the various types of **comets**—occupy a more sublime position in the human aerial medium, specifically within the **spirits of life**. It follows that they do not merely affect the "seeds" of such meteors in a deadly way when they are scattered in the macrocosmic air and breathed in by humans, but because of their elevated position, they even penetrate the essence of the vital force. From this arise plagues and pestilential fevers, and all contagious diseases. From this we are also taught by experience that the appearance of a comet usually indicates decay and a morbid disposition not only for humans, but also for plants and fruits; thus, a prognosis is usually made regarding plague and famine. Furthermore, we see that the minimum duration of a comet’s appearance is seven days, which is also the time in which pestilential diseases—and especially the plague and pestilential fevers—tend to reach their end within seven days; for the crisis of a very acute disease is measured by a continuation of this kind.

In the human "air" <note>The "aerial" part of the human spirit or breath</note>, therefore, three distinct regions may be perceived: the location compared to the **highest region** of the air, in which similar contents are produced; a location likened to the **middle region** with its contents or meteors adapted to it; and the **lowest location** assigned to thick spirits and humors. The solid body of man, however, corresponds to the **Earth**. Therefore, just as the earth is subject to many accidents—namely, sulfurous flames, hot waters, and other such things—so too do "gums" resembling amber, sulfurous inflammations, and other such things occur in the human body.

On the Formal Cause of Meteors. 129

In this description, we establish the material cause of the <term>prester</term> <note>original: *presteris*; a term used in ancient and Renaissance meteorology for a "fiery whirlwind" or lightning-stroke accompanied by a vortex.</note> to be a fiery or sulfurous rain; however, we identify its efficient cause <note>the agent or "builder" that brings something into existence</note> as Jehovah himself, inasmuch as He creates it as if anew from nothing, or brings it forth from the treasury of God, which is the invisible treasury of the air. Its formal cause <note>the "shape" or defining characteristic that makes a thing what it is</note> is explained by the fact that it is called a rain not of water, but of fire and sulfur. Finally, we have expressed its end <note>its final purpose</note> in that it is usually brought forth for the punishment and destruction of the wicked.

By the testimony of the Holy Scriptures, we can prove all these causes of the <term>prester</term> in this manner. First, in the writings of the Royal Psalmist, we find: *Jehovah shall rain upon the wicked coals, fire and sulfur, and a wind joined with various storms,* <note>original: *prestere*; Psalm 11:6</note>. Here the Prophet expresses the matter and form, as well as the efficient cause and the end. He identifies the matter in his mention of "coals, fire, and sulfur," and through these words, he distinguishes the <term>prester</term> from ordinary water-rain by a sufficiently clear form. Furthermore, he sets the efficient cause not as the sun—which is merely a created thing—but as Jehovah the Creator, who acts directly in all things. Finally, he establishes the end: to torment the wicked and deliver them to death. David writes elsewhere of the effect of such a meteor: *As fire burns the forest, as a flame sets the mountains ablaze, so pursue them with your tempest, and terrify them with your whirlwind.* Here the Prophet seems to take the <term>prester</term> as a species of whirlwind. Similarly, Moses describes the effect of such a meteor in these express words: *The land is so burnt with sulfur and salt that it can neither be sown nor sprout, nor can any herb grow upon it,* <note>Deuteronomy 29:23</note>. Finally, in Genesis, the components of our aforementioned description are confirmed in plain and open words: *Jehovah (says the Text) sent down from the heavens a rain of sulfur and fire upon the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, which overthrew the cities and the entire plain, and all the inhabitants and the growth of the ground, because of the wickedness of those dwelling there.*

Therefore, it will be most clearly apparent to any wise person who diligently considers these things we have brought forward how vain is the opinion of the Pagan philosophers and their Christian followers in this matter. Furthermore, when the text says "from the heavens," it understands the "inner chambers of the air," which we previously declared to be the treasury-ark of all meteors; this is confirmed by these words of the high priest: *Jehovah shall open to you his excellent treasury, the heavens, giving rain in its season,* <note>Deuteronomy 28:12</note>. And it is said elsewhere: *Have you entered the treasuries of the snow? Or have you inspected the treasuries of the hail?* <note>Job 38:22</note> and so it is with the rest. In these places, it is certain that God possesses treasury-arks for every species of meteor, and that they are produced from hidden power into manifest action according to the Creator's pleasure. Surely this dispute of ours regarding the investigation of such meteors should not seem irrelevant to the wise, for in it—contrary to the opinion of the philosophers of this age—we attribute their generation to the Great and Sovereign God, Jehovah, and not to accidental causes in nature or to created things such as the sun and stars, etc.

For since it is certain, and confirmed by the sacred text, that the world—by means of such a fiery deluge—shall be deprived of its present form, destroyed, and purified on the Day of Final Judgment, we think it should be diligently considered among learned Christians that the error of the Pagan philosophers should be driven into exile from the Christian state, beyond the Hyperborean mountains, and handed over to the perpetual oblivion of good men. This error is namely: that the cause of such a meteor (by which the world must perish and be destroyed at the end—that is, be changed and purged from its prior form by purification) usually arises from the earth by the heat of the sun and stars, and not from God, the Father of all wonders, to whom be praise and glory. Was it not for this reason said: *that the Son of Man shall come from the east to the west, in the manner of lightning and a consuming fire?* <note>Matthew 24</note>. So also Jehovah is called *a consuming fire, before whose sight nothing can endure, for the mountains melt like wax,* etc. <note>Deuteronomy 4</note>. And yet the Peripatetics <note>followers of Aristotle</note> and the Christians who follow them wish for such power to arise solely from "imaginary exhalations"—but let us return to the point.

Since the matter of the <term>turbo</term> <note>whirlwind</note> or <term>typhon</term> <note>a violent storm-wind</note> is the same as that of the <term>prester</term>, though it is observed to be sent from the heavens in a different form and smaller quantity, we therefore assign to it the following description, in agreement with the Holy Bible. First, we divide it into the "fiery or inflamed whirlwind" and the "non-fiery whirlwind," which rotates dust, straw, and sometimes larger objects in a circle.

The inflamed whirlwind we describe thus from holy testimony:

An inflamed whirlwind is a fiery wind, revolved into a globe or wheel, which—proceeding from its inner chamber by divine power, whether from the northern or southern quarter, or even from the Southwest—has sometimes been made the vehicle of Jehovah. It is like a tabernacle from which He chooses to appear to the saints, to speak to them, sometimes even to snatch them up to Himself in heaven, and most often to send forth His vengeance upon the wicked. Here, the material cause is wind or fiery air; the formal cause is that inflamed air revolved into a wheel; the place is its "inner chamber," that is, a cloud appropriate for its generation; the efficient cause is the power of Jehovah, by which it is brought forth from His own treasures; the end is that it may be the seat of the divine essence, and as it were a tent from which He is accustomed to speak with His saints at times, and frequently to pour out punishments upon the wicked. We have also expressed the quarters of the world from which it usually proceeds. All these things we defend by the authority of the sacred context.

# On the Formal Cause of Meteors. 135

## CHAPTER XVI.

### Part One.

### Concerning the Rainbow, or the celestial arc.

By the Peripatetics <note>original: "Peripateticis"; the followers of Aristotle, who famously taught while walking about</note>, the Rainbow is said to be an arc of various colors in a dewy, dark, and hollow cloud, appearing to the eyes of spectators from the reflection of the rays of the sun positioned opposite to it. They say that it cannot be otherwise than that its shape is arched or semicircular, although it is certain, and proven by experience, that such an arc—according to the testimony of Holy Scripture—sometimes circles the heavens in a complete circuit, just as is demonstrated to the eye in our meteorographic mirror <note>likely a reference to a specific diagram or optical instrument used by the author</note>.

* In this description of theirs, therefore, they establish the material cause <term>material cause: the physical matter or "stuff" out of which something is made</term> from which (or in which) it is made as the dewy, dark, and hollow cloud. They explain the formal cause <term>formal cause: the specific shape, pattern, or essence that defines a thing</term> by saying it is a multi-colored arc. They make the efficient cause <term>efficient cause: the agent or force that brings something into being</term> the solar rays, from whose reflection it appears to the eyes of those watching.

But we truly gather from the text of the Holy Scriptures that the Rainbow can be described by the Christian Philosopher in this manner:

The Rainbow is the circle or arc of GOD, most glorious in its splendor, which the hand of the Most High has so extended, and placed in the clouds on a day of rain, so that it might be a sign of the covenant <note>A reference to Genesis 9, where the rainbow is the "bow in the clouds" signifying God's promise to Noah</note>

<summary>This page defines the rainbow by comparing the Aristotelian (Peripatetic) scientific view—focusing on reflection and clouds—with a Christian philosophical view that emphasizes the rainbow as a divine sign of a covenant.</summary>
<keywords>rainbow, iris, Peripatetics, Aristotle, material cause, formal cause, efficient cause, Holy Scripture, meteorology, covenant</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on meteorological phenomena, specifically transitioning from the physical properties of the atmosphere to the optical and spiritual nature of the rainbow (Iris). It challenges the traditional Aristotelian view of reflection in favor of a more mystical and experimental understanding.</meta>

->136 Section I. Part IV. Book III. Member III.<-

...from which it follows that, contrary to the opinions of the **Peripatetic philosophers** <note>original: "Philosophorum Peripateticorum"; these were followers of Aristotle who taught while walking in the Lyceum</note>, it is not required for the rainbow to be formed in the hollow of a dark cloud. Indeed, the rainbow is observed most frequently to appear in air that is sufficiently dense yet clear and transparent; <margin>1</margin> for this reason, one may even discern a mountain or a forest through it. The sacred text seems to address this misty air where it is said by the wise man: *Ecclesiasticus 50:8. A rainbow shining among the clouds of glory*, and other testimonies of Holy Scripture also seem to speak of such a cloud, namely the misty air. Therefore, the Rainbow appears to emerge among dense clouds, and the eye perceives it in the misty or dewy air. 

And although some philosophers, and indeed experts in optics, wish to discuss and debate the variety of the Rainbow's colors in their own fashion—saying that the diversity of colors arises from variations in both the cloud and the light, and that thin water in the dewy cloud, otherwise bright air, and dark clouds must all concur for the creation of different colors—they claim all these things, when irradiated by the sun, provide different colors: namely crimson, green, yellow, citron-yellow, red, sea-green, or azure. (**Aristotle** seems to treat these matters in Book 3 of his *Meteorology*). Nevertheless, if we wish to consider the matter a little more accurately, we see that it behaves differently than they supposed. For instance, the colors of the rainbow are commonly produced without those specific mediums and in other subjects, as **Roger Bacon** <note>An English Franciscan friar and philosopher (c. 1214–1292) known for his emphasis on empiricism and early optics</note> teaches in his book on experimental science, and as common experience also shows.

Indeed, such colors are observed to appear in many lower things: for if we take **hexagonal stones** <note>original: "lapides... hexagonios"; likely quartz or beryl crystals</note> from India or Ireland and hold them against the rays of the sun penetrating through a window or some opening into a shadow or shaded air, we will perceive near the rays all the colors of the rainbow in the same order as they are arranged in the heavenly bow. Therefore, it is certain that such colors can be produced without the aforementioned conditions of clouds; thus, it does not seem to follow that these colors are brought to light merely because of the reflection of solar rays in a dewy, hollow, and dark cloud. Nor does it follow of necessity that the solar rays striking directly are the sole cause producing such a variety of colors. For, according to the testimony of Roger Bacon, if an operator takes the said hexagonal stone and moves into a somewhat darker place, and applies the stone to his half-closed eye, he will immediately discern the said colors of the rainbow in the air. 

There are some, therefore, who believe that colors of this kind are produced by a property of that stone; but truly, this is false, because these colors appear in both shaded and luminous air when using either a crystal or a well-polished glass body reduced to a triangular shape. Furthermore, such colors sometimes appear on the oars of a boat when they are wet with dew and the droplets are dripping as they are lifted from the water; the same thing happens when water is violently thrown against the rays of the sun. Yet, as has been said, it is not necessary that we have the presence of the sun for such an appearance, since it often happens that even at night, in the absence of the sun, these colors are observed appearing around a candle. Nevertheless, we admit that it is necessary for some light to be present, without which we cannot discern anything colored, much less colors that cannot be seen without a colored object. But as pertains to the subject in which these colors are visible, we say it can be the air itself imbued with light; for I remember that in the morning, while lying in bed, I clearly and for a long time perceived the colors of the rainbow in and near the solar rays.

Therefore, the **efficient cause** <note>The primary source of change or rest; in this context, the force that actually makes the rainbow happen</note> of these marvelous colors is without doubt more occult and hidden than can be easily comprehended by the Heathen philosophers, or even by their followers among the Christians of this age. For **GOD**, who is everything and in everything, and who fills the spirits of the world everywhere with His brilliance (though it be invisible), is the cause of such a wonderful thing in nature; He is accustomed to reveal Himself to men through signs, through colors, through lightning, and through infinite other ways. 

In moist nature, this light is called by **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure associated with a syncretism of the Greek god Hermes and the Egyptian god Thoth, credited with the Hermetic writings</note> (*Pimander*, Book 1) the "Voice of Light," or the **Word**, which, standing by moist nature, cherished it. And another, immersing himself deeply in the mysteries of nature (*On the Chemical Art*, Chapter 9), says that this hidden nature is a certain infinite power, procreating like from like, increasing and nourishing all things, and for this reason possessing the names of all things within itself. It is of no color, yet it participates in and is the effecter of all colors; it is the fertile mother of all qualities and things. From this he concludes that this nature is GOD, and GOD is this uncreated nature—the created/creating moistness that nourishes. 

The **Platonists** <note>Followers of Plato's philosophy</note> recognize this as the **Soul of the World** <note>original: "mundi animam"; the Anima Mundi, a spiritual essence that encompasses all living things on Earth</note>, existing invisibly within its whole and every part, much like the human soul in its body. **Zoroaster** (with whom **Heraclitus of Ephesus** also seems to agree) calls this the **invisible fire** from which all things are begotten. Other Hebrew Doctors hold that it is that fiery vigor which the **Spirit of Elohim** <note>original: "spiritus Elohim"; the Spirit of God from Genesis 1:2</note>—which is the fiery love that was moved over the waters—brought forth into them, and consequently dispersed everywhere throughout the world, though invisibly. For according to the testimony of Saint Peter, *The heavens and earth were formerly of water, and subsisting through water by the Word of GOD (2 Peter 3)*; that is, by the primary emanation from the throne of divinity, by means of which *all things were made, and without it, nothing was made (John 1)*.

142                                  **A Clear Exposition**

...we estimate: but indeed, we believe the upper region to be the most vast and remarkably spacious; however, we think the region situated between these two—the middle—is moderate in its dimensions between those extremes. In these specific regions are included the principal arguments of our intention (as has been said), and we have judged that this must be considered by you above all, and placed before your eyes, regarding the various seats and positions of meteors <note>In this period, "meteors" referred to all atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, clouds, and lightning, following the Aristotelian tradition.</note>.

In the upper region, we have ordained that the divine act and the instruments or ministers—in and through whom all things in these lower parts, and indeed in the heavens above, are perfected—must be distinguished according to the strength of our understanding. Concerning these things, as they are the beginnings of all things whether perfectly or imperfectly mixed, we shall indeed speak lightly and briefly in this place, descending from the vertex of the mirror to the base, since mention has been made of them abundantly in both the preceding and following sections, to the honor of GOD, the creator of all, and the education of man, who is the end and perfection of all.

Since all things created in the world, whether they be simple or arisen from simple things (such as Angels, as they are "otherness" and forged from two; the stars; and also among the sublunary bodies, especially the imperfectly mixed things which are composed in and from the air; and finally the perfectly mixed, such as animals, vegetables, and minerals) are composed of a radiant form—whether it be apparent or hidden—and matter, as the subject from which they are composed; of these, it is the role of the latter to be passive, and the former to act. Without these qualities, nothing in the world could exist or reach the goal of perfection toward which all things tend. Thus, in the first place, those things come to be considered: namely, what the source and beginning is in the motion of continuous action, from which various acts are flowed and disseminated everywhere through the world; and then, what the immediate ministers or organs of the primary actor are, through which and in which he acts, or pours out the acts of his emanation. And then, we think it must be considered with diligent intuition what the principal subjects in the world are—both in the ethereal heaven and in the air (in which all kinds of meteors, about which we here principally intend, are usually procreated)—and finally in the water and the earth, around which the aforementioned acts of God are observed to act and be engaged.

In the first or superior place, we find God himself in the immense and infinite dimension of his divinity, described as if in some way by letters—since he can never be depicted by an image or comprehended by the human mind in his infinity—which it pleases us to signify or express in that place through the word *Ensoph* <note>The Hebrew *Ein Sof*, meaning "The Infinite" or "Without End," representing God before manifestation.</note> along with the Kabbalists and more secret Theologians. This signifies Infinity, which they asserted to be the unique fountain of life and divine essence; namely infinity, without which nothing lives and nothing is, for all things proceed from the One. And this unique fountain (into whose secrets it is not possible to penetrate) they—not without consideration—make into a double spring, namely natural and spiritual, from which the living waters proceed. These descend by way of emanation, first through a stream into the radiant paternal gate called *Elion Cheter* <note>original: *Elion Cheter*; the Hebrew *Elyon Keter*, meaning "The Most High Crown."</note>, that is, the supreme crown; and then afterward into the son, *Hochma* or wisdom <note>original: *Hochma*; the Hebrew *Chokhmah*.</note>. Hence the royal Psalmist says: *With you is the fountain of life*. From which it was right to gather that GOD, in his innermost essence, is outside of all things and beyond the cavity of the world, nor can he be comprehended by the sharp edge of the mind. Nevertheless, through various breathing-holes, which are the *Sephirotic* <note>original: *Sephiroticae*; referring to the ten Sephirot or divine emanations of the Kabbalah.</note> enumerations or radiant gates, he disperses and disseminates various radiant emanations into the world, distinct from one another by property, downward everywhere through the cavity of the world. These emanations, taking on a mundane spirit, are accustomed to take on the names and properties of Angels. The first three of these, from the number of ten, are ordered for the forging of the world's regions, heavens, and elements; the first, the crown, is ascribed to the Father; the second, called wisdom, to the Son; and prudence <note>Likely referring to *Binah* (Understanding).</note> to the Holy Spirit. This also the royal Prophet seems to argue in this speech: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and all their power by the spirit from his mouth*; where the Lord is the father, emitting the word or wisdom, by means of which heaven and earth were created from the waters (as St. Peter testifies), and by the spirit from both, all power is in them. Seven other emanations, however, are received and, as it were, imbibed by the seven remaining Angelic spirits, by means of which the said Angels are informed, and act and work according to the property of the Divine name by which they are filled, into those mundane subjects disposed anywhere through the spacious world; and these are those angels who are said to preside over the Seven Planets, about which more will be said below.

As for those angelic or spiritual receptacles or organs, which are ordained by God to receive the species of divine influxes: for the better understanding of the readers, we shall explain them in this manner, in few words, along with the channels of the influxes, the orders of angels who first receive them, and finally to which spheres of the celestial region they lead them as part of their office.

First, therefore, it must be known and observed with diligent intellect, that from the infinite fountain of immense divinity called *Ensoph*, ten radiant emanations (according to the intentions of the Kabbalists) flow out through as many channels differing in property. These are poured out and emanate everywhere into the world according to the will of God, primarily into ten various orders of Angels and saints. From these, ten Archangels (counting the soul of the Messiah among them), created by GOD for this business, receive each of them those emanations as radiant influxes from each order. For almost all Theosophers agree in this: that as the orders of Angels are superior...

### Of the Meteorological Mirror, 143

The higher orders receive the light, or a luminous emanation, directly from God, and in this way they emit and manifest it to those of the lower orders. In this, Dionysius <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, an influential 5th-century theologian who wrote "The Celestial Hierarchy."</note>, Basil, Isidore, Gregory, and others agree. 

Similarly, from a serious study of the Holy Bible, the more "secret" theologians <note>referring to practitioners of mystical or esoteric theology</note> have observed ten distinct properties in **GOD**. They have also perceived various names of **GOD** relating to these properties, which were assigned by the prophets and patriarchs. Thus, to each of these emanations, a specific Angel is assigned, who holds a sole and primary duty concerning that specific property of **GOD** to which he was destined from the beginning.

And the **Archangel** <note>A reference to Archangelus of Borgonovo, a 16th-century commentator on Cabalistic texts.</note> in his *Commentary on the Cabalistic Dogmas* seems to assert that it is into this order that the influxes from **Beauty** <note>Tipherith</note> are directed, which indeed can also seem probable on account of its bright, clear, and beautiful condition: inasmuch as in it the light of **God** shines wonderfully. But we follow **Dionysius** <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite</note> and **Isidore** here: This influx is received from this order by the good Angel **Haniel**, and is carried down into the sphere of **Venus**, by whose presence and power good influences, pleasing to the human race, are scattered everywhere through the sublunary air, water, and earth. By its presence also, thin clouds and sometimes thin sifting rain are usually produced; hence it is also that this Planet, namely Venus, is called the <term>Lesser Fortune</term> <note>original: "Fortunium minus"; Venus was considered a "benefic" planet bringing harmony and pleasure.</note> by Astrologers.

From there, having been sent later into the sublunary region, it sometimes produces rapid winds in the air, which are not infrequently associated with heavy showers and rains. Furthermore, this influx is observed to act in various ways in man, namely it renders the senses good, makes the wit sharp, and the memory fruitful.

   The Ninth is called **The Almighty** <note>original: SADAI / Shaddai</note> whose bright gate is the **Foundation** <note>original: Iesod / Yesod</note> through which, descending, it passes into the order of **Angels**, from which it is committed to the Guardian **Gabriel**, who directs it into the sphere of the **Moon**, which rains down moist and cold influences into the air, water, and earth, producing various and multiform impressions in them, namely winds, rains, and other things of this kind.

   Finally, the Tenth is called **The Lord** <note>original: ADONAI</note>, that is, Lord, whose channel is the **Kingdom** <note>original: Malchut / Malkuth</note>, from which this emanation descends into the sphere of souls (as the Cabalists will have it), led by the **Soul of the Messiah**, which at last is carried down from it into the elements, where for the most part severe effects are produced on account of man's disobedience.

   Here, however, I would have you know in passing, according to the intentions of the **Magicians** and **Cabalists**, that each of the aforesaid angels is a great Prince, having power of much liberty, insofar as it is in their offices to dispose these gifts of **God**, or these properties of His, either mercifully or severely according to His will, among the creatures of this sublunary world. And their powers seem to grow more according to their common and natural or accustomed disposition in the annual course, in the dominion of their planets and signs, and consequently in their ordained times, namely years, months, days, and hours, and in the elements and parts of the world, and the winds appropriated to them. And certainly, to speak more truly, the dominion belongs neither to the signs nor the planets, but is in respect of the more abundant divine efflux, which comes to it more at one time than another, according to the divine will. Consequently, the Angel or **Intelligence** of the planet or star is like its internal spirit moving it, whose central soul is that very emanation of divinity, by which it is continually intoxicated as if with divine nectar. Therefore, it is poorly said by those skilled in Magic that the Angels act in the dominion of a sign or planet, but rather that the sign and planet are stronger or more powerful according to the greater or lesser strength of their Intelligence in the divine emanation which it receives. Furthermore, it is also to be understood that every one of these powerful Angels (seven of whom are said to stand before the face of God) rules over many legions, with which he is accustomed to act both in heaven and in the elementary region.

   But now we have arrived at the purpose we have at hand: namely, the exposition and explanation of the forms, locations, and qualities depicted in our **Meteorographic Mirror** <note>original: "Catoptro nostro Meteorographico"; likely a reference to an illustrated chart or a specific optical instrument designed by the author.</note>. Regarding their location, we find it to be either common or specific. We call the "common" location the entire space of air between the ethereal heaven and the earth. We have established three regions of this whole and common air as "specific" locations. We see the upper region filled with <term>comets</term> <note>In this period, "meteors" and "comets" were considered atmospheric phenomena occurring within the Earth's air, not in deep space.</note> of various kinds and differing shapes, along with "chasms" and "burning beams," about which we will speak only briefly here, as they are treated more fully elsewhere.
   As there are various species of comets, so too have the Philosophers assigned names to them that match their appearance.
   Therefore, they called the first species the **Spear**, as it is stretched out in length.
   The **Sword** <note>original: "Xiphias"</note> is a shorter spear, and this species of comet is tapered to a sharp point.
   The **Mercurial** is a comet that is somewhat bluish from heat, small in size, and having a tiny, long tail.
   The **Soldier** <note>original: "Miles"</note> is so named because it has a "Martial" <note>Reddish, like the planet Mars.</note> color; this comet is also tailed, as you have it delineated in the **Mirror**.
   The **Aurora** has the appearance of a star, but it excels every star in its clarity and splendor.
   The **Rose** is a comet large and round in size, which seems to display and bear a human face.
   The **Pincers** <note>original: "Tenaculum"</note> is a comet which, standing as if upon a fiery base, is tailed in a wondrous manner.
   The **Black** comet is of a dark color, endowed with a short and brief tail, and it appears to be adorned in some way with very little "hair" <note>The word "comet" comes from the Greek word for hair; the author is describing the thinness of its coma or tail.</note>.
   The **Horned** <note>original: "Ceratias"</note> is a comet named for its horned shape or the form of its fire.
   There are also other "ignited meteors" which are sometimes visible in this region, which we nevertheless do not call comets at all. Just as comets are set ablaze in such a way that they are not quickly extinguished, these other apparitions—such as the **Chasm**, the **Beam**, and **flying sparks**—are less so, being born from a less firm and more inconstant matter or spirit. But since we have spoken of these before and have also explained their forms in our **Mirror**, we have decided not to make a longer discourse on them in this place.
   For the other meteors, both the luminous and the dark, I judge that you should be referred—without further explanation here regarding their forms and locations—primarily to the inspection of our **Mirror**, and for their order, to the previously mentioned table or classification, for the sake of brevity.

   **Regarding Meteors which are seen, but are not what they seem to be.**

   Now, however, we come to those meteors which exhibit a certain image or shape in the air, and yet are not the things they appear to be. Truly, since this will appear difficult and hard to consider at first glance to the unlearned and those unskilled in the science of optics, we have therefore expressed the logic of those appearances in the "perspective" manner in our **Meteorographic Mirror**. We have done this with proper and consistent demonstrations, so that you might reach a certain knowledge of such visions in the air more easily and without great fatigue. In this task of demonstrating, I confess that I follow and imitate the doctrine of **Witelo** <note>original: "Vitellionis"; Witelo was a 13th-century friar and physicist famous for his influential work on optics.</note> regarding the nature of vision. By this we are taught that we see through the action of a visible form upon the eye, and the "passion" <note>In the sense of a passive reception or impression.</note> of the sight by such a form. Moreover, these kinds of meteors—the logic of which we gather solely from the science of optics, since they are not what they appear to be—are the **Parhelia** <note>Mock suns.</note>. These occur when the sun is rising or setting, at an angle, in the lower part of a cloud and in the lowest part of the region of air. They are images or likenesses of the Sun or the Moon which are represented in a dewy cloud, not otherwise than what is seen in water or a mirror. We show the logic of this vision through "pyramidal lines" <note>Visual cones or rays.</note> from the point of sight to the objects of the Sun and Moon in the lower part of the cloud, just as is demonstrated in our **Mirror**.
